title: Fix supplier ID type in SetSuppliersCommand
issue_title: TypeError when saving a product with a supplier ID returned as string
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20type%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

When PDO returns numeric database values as strings, saving a product with an associated supplier can trigger a `TypeError`:

```text
PrestaShop\PrestaShop\Core\Domain\Supplier\ValueObject\SupplierId::__construct():
Argument #1 ($supplierId) must be of type int, string given

called in:
src/Core/Domain/Product/Supplier/Command/SetSuppliersCommand.php
```

The issue occurs while supplier IDs are processed by `SetSuppliersCommand`.

Depending on the PDO/database environment, a supplier ID can be returned as a numeric string, for example `"1"`, while `SupplierId` expects an `int`.

This is another occurrence of the numeric-string type issue tracked in #38735.

A similar occurrence was reported in #42447 and is handled separately by #42475 for the product grid and product pack flows.


### Steps to reproduce

The problem can be reproduced by forcing PDO to return fetched numeric values as strings.

Temporarily modify `classes/db/DbPDO.php` in the `getPDO()` method.

Replace:

```php
return new PDO(
    $dsn,
    $user,
    $password,
    $options
);
```

with:

```php
$pdo = new PDO(
    $dsn,
    $user,
    $password,
    $options
);

$pdo->setAttribute(PDO::ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES, true);

return $pdo;
```

This modification is only required to reproduce the affected PDO behavior and must not be committed.

Then:

1. Make sure at least one supplier exists.
2. Associate the supplier with a product.
3. Go to **BO > Catalog > Products**.
4. Edit the product.
5. Make any editable change.
6. Save the product.
7. Verify that a `TypeError` is triggered in `SupplierId::__construct()` because the supplier ID is provided as a string.

After the test, revert the temporary change to `classes/db/DbPDO.php`.

title: Fix #42395: Prevent template variables from being overwritten
issue_title: `actionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore` variables are overwritten in `FrontController::assignGeneralPurposeVariables()`
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20type%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments


There is a regression in `FrontController::assignGeneralPurposeVariables()` affecting the `actionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore` hook.

This hook receives `$templateVars` by reference and is intended to allow modules to define or override template variables before the core assigns its general-purpose variables.

However, after the hook is executed, `$templateVars` is completely reassigned:

```php
$templateVars = [
    'cart' => $this->cart_presenter->present($cart, true),
    'currency' => $this->getTemplateVarCurrency(),
    'customer' => $this->getTemplateVarCustomer(),
    'country' => $this->objectPresenter->present($this->context->country),
    'language' => $this->objectPresenter->present($this->context->language),
    'page' => $this->getTemplateVarPage(),
    'shop' => $this->getTemplateVarShop(),
    'core_js_public_path' => $this->getCoreJsPublicPath(),
    'urls' => $this->getTemplateVarUrls(),
    'configuration' => $this->getTemplateVarConfiguration(),
    'field_required' => $this->context->customer->validateFieldsRequiredDatabase(),
    'breadcrumb' => $this->getBreadcrumb(),
    'link' => $this->context->link,
    'time' => time(),
    'static_token' => Tools::getToken(false),
    'token' => Tools::getToken(),
    'debug' => _PS_MODE_DEV_,
];
```

As a consequence, any variable added by a module through `actionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore` is lost.

For example:

```php
public function hookActionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore(array $params): void
{
    $params['templateVars']['test_variable'] = 'test value';
}
```

`test_variable` is no longer available in Smarty after the hook execution.

This appears to be a regression from the previous implementation, where core variables were assigned individually using the existing value when already provided:

```php
$templateVars['cart'] = $templateVars['cart'] ?? $this->cart_presenter->present($cart);
```

That implementation preserved variables added by modules and also allowed modules to provide a value before the core calculated it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install the [issueactionfrontcontrollersetvariablesbefore.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31307869/issueactionfrontcontrollersetvariablesbefore.zip) module.
2. Go to the Front Office.
3. In the footer, you should see the value value. Instead, **Variable not set** is displayed, indicating that the variable added by the module is not available in the template.

### Expected behavior


Variables added to `$templateVars` from `actionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore` should still be available in Smarty after `assignGeneralPurposeVariables()` has completed.

For example:

```php
$params['templateVars']['test_variable'] = 'test value';
```

should make the following usable from a Smarty template:

```smarty
{$test_variable}
```

Existing core variables provided by the hook should also not be overwritten, consistently with the previous behavior of this hook.

### Actual Result

_No response_

### PrestaShop version where the bug happens

9.0.0

### How have you installed PrestaShop

_No response_

### PHP version(s) where the bug happened

_No response_

title: Order confirmation email ignores the order state's "Attach invoice PDF to email" setting
issue_title: Order confirmation email ignores the order state's "Attach invoice PDF to email" checkbox setting
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20type%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

Order confirmation email attaches the invoice PDF based on the order state's `invoice` flag instead of `pdf_invoice`. That meeans that unchecking **"Attach invoice PDF to email"** on an order status is silently ignored for the order confirmation email, as long as that status has the *Invoice* toggle  enabled.

The result is that on order confirmation, the customer gets an invoice attachment even if that option is explicitly disabled in the order state's configuration

### Steps to reproduce

1. Go to **Shop Parameters > Order Settings > Statuses**.
2. Pick the status your payment method validates orders into (e.g. *Processing* or *Payment accepted*), and make sure the invoice toggle is on.
3. Edit the said order state, and **uncheck "Attach invoice PDF to email"**. 
4. Place an order through that payment method on the front office.

### Expected behavior

No invoice attachment in email since the **Attach PDF to email** is unchecked
The `order_conf` attachment should honour `pdf_invoice`, consistent with the field's help text ("This will attach invoice PDF to the sent email, if it exists. If it doesn't, it will have no effect.")

### Actual Result

The order confirmation email received by the customer has the invoice PDF attached

### PrestaShop version where the bug happens

9.2.0-beta1

### How have you installed PrestaShop

PrestaShop 9.2 Classic Beta 1 zip package

### PHP version(s) where the bug happened

8.4

title: Fix Pack::getQuantity ignoring 'Decrement pack only' stock type
issue_title: Pack stock type "Decrement pack only" is ignored by Pack::getQuantity() - empty() treats STOCK_TYPE_PACK_ONLY (0) as "Default"
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20type%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

A pack whose per-product stock behavior is explicitly set to **"Decrement pack only"** (`pack_stock_type = 0`, `PackStockType::STOCK_TYPE_PACK_ONLY`) is treated as if it was set to "Default" by `Pack::getQuantity()`, so its displayed/available quantity is resolved using the **global** `PS_PACK_STOCK_TYPE` configuration instead of the pack's own setting.

**Root cause** - `classes/Pack.php`, `Pack::getQuantity()`:

https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/classes/Pack.php#L293

```php
// If no pack stock or shop default, set it from configuration
if (empty($packStockType) || $packStockType == self::STOCK_TYPE_DEFAULT) {
    $packStockType = Configuration::get('PS_PACK_STOCK_TYPE');
}
```

`STOCK_TYPE_PACK_ONLY === 0` and `empty(0) === true`, so an explicit "Decrement pack only" is indistinguishable from "not set" and always falls back to the global configuration. The per-pack value 0 only "works" when the global default happens to be "Decrement pack only" as well. Values 1 ("products only"), 2 ("both") and 3 ("default") behave correctly.

The same line is present in all maintained branches:
- `develop`: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/classes/Pack.php#L293
- `8.2.x`: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/8.2.x/classes/Pack.php#L311
- `9.0.0`: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/9.0.0/classes/Pack.php#L313

**Why this is more than a display glitch** - the stock *decrement* path uses exact comparisons and DOES honor the per-pack value 0 (`StockManager::updatePackQuantity()`):

https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/src/Core/Stock/StockManager.php#L45-L70

So for a pack set to "Decrement pack only" while the shop default is "Decrement products in pack only" (or "both"):
- placing an order decrements the **pack's own** stock (per-pack setting honored),
- but the FO product page, listings, and availability checks (`Product::getQuantity()` → `Pack::getQuantity()`, `Pack::isInStock()`) display a quantity computed **from the pack's components** (per-pack setting ignored, global used).

The displayed availability is therefore computed from stock that is never decremented by sales of this pack, and the two numbers drift apart with every order. Since `Pack::isInStock()` relies on the same method, cart availability checks use the wrong mode as well - this may be (part of) the root cause of the overselling symptoms reported in #26728.

**Suggested fix** - stop treating the legitimate value 0 as "unset", while keeping the legacy NULL/empty-string fallback that `empty()` presumably guarded:

```php
if ($packStockType === null || $packStockType === '' || (int) $packStockType == self::STOCK_TYPE_DEFAULT) {
    $packStockType = Configuration::get('PS_PACK_STOCK_TYPE');
}
```

**Related:** #26728 (open symptom report: overselling with "Decrement pack only" / "Decrement both"), #19846 (pack stock EPIC), PR #35372 (last refactor of this method, 8.1.5 - the `empty()` condition was kept unchanged).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh PrestaShop install (reproduced on 8.1.7; the affected code is identical on `8.2.x`, `9.0.0` and `develop`), stock management enabled.
2. In BO: Shop Parameters > Product Settings > set **"Default pack stock management"** to **"Decrement products in pack only"**.
3. Create standard product A with quantity **10** and standard product B with quantity **20**.
4. Create a pack containing **2 × A** and **1 × B**. Set the pack's own quantity to **1** and set the pack's stock management option (product page > Quantities) to **"Decrement pack only"**.
5. Open the pack's product page in the front office (or call `Product::getQuantity($idPack)` / check the displayed availability).
6. (Divergence part) Place an order for 1 pack and compare which stock was decremented vs. which stock the FO displays.

### Expected behavior

The pack's available quantity should be **1** - its own stock - because the pack explicitly overrides the shop default with "Decrement pack only". Ordering the pack decrements the pack's own stock, consistently with what is displayed.

### Actual Result

The FO displays quantity **5** - `min(floor(10/2), floor(20/1))` - i.e. the quantity computed from the pack's components according to the **global** "Decrement products in pack only" setting. The per-pack "Decrement pack only" is silently ignored.

After ordering 1 pack: the pack's own stock drops 1 → 0 (decrement path honors the per-pack setting), while the FO still displays 5. Displayed availability is permanently detached from the stock that sales actually decrement.

### PrestaShop version where the bug happens

develop (verified also on 8.2.x, 9.0.0 and 8.1.7)

### How have you installed PrestaShop

Docker image prestashop/prestashop:8.1.7, clean auto-install; code additionally inspected on branches 8.2.x / 9.0.0 / develop

### PHP version(s) where the bug happened

8.1

title: Keep word separation when stripping HTML for the search index
issue_title: Issue with search indexing after HTML stripping (concatenated words and indexing error)
issue_body:
### Prerequisites - [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). - [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug. ### Describe the bug and add attachments During product search indexing, two issues occur when the text being indexed (e.g., product description) contains HTML that is stripped without adding spaces between the resulting text segments. The issue occurs both when content is inserted manually into the database (e.g., via phpMyAdmin or MySQL client) and when it is imported through a module. --- ### Current behavior **Case 1** -- If the following string is saved in the product description (all on one line): ```
  • Position: out
  • File format: mp3
``` when rebuilding the search index, Prestashop throws an error and the indexing process stops. ### Case 2 -- If the product description contains the following string (again, all on one line): ```
  • Position: in
  • File format: mp3
``` - indexing completes without errors, - but Prestashop incorrectly indexes the word `infile` instead of the two separate words `in` and `file`. Running a query like: ```sql SELECT * FROM `ps_search_word` WHERE `word` LIKE 'infile'; ``` shows that the incorrect term `infile` has been stored in the index. --- Problem analysis --- In both cases, the root cause appears to be the HTML removal process, which strips tags but does not insert spaces between the extracted text segments. As a result, strings like “Position: in” and “File format: mp3” are merged without separation, producing incorrect search tokens and, in some cases (e.g. with the word out), triggering an error during the indexing process. ### Expected behavior - Indexing should complete without errors, regardless of the textual content of the product description. - Text resulting from stripped HTML should maintain proper word separation (e.g. `in File` should produce two separate indexed words: `in` and `file`). ### Steps to reproduce ### Case 1 (indexing error) 1. Enable debug mode. 2. Manually edit a product description (via phpMyAdmin or MySQL client) and insert the following content in a single line: ```
  • Position: out
  • File format: mp3
``` 3. Go to **Shop Parameters > Search > Search** and click **Re-build the entire index**. 4. An error should appear during the indexing process. **Case 2 (incorrect word indexed)** Enable debug mode. 1. Manually edit a product description (via phpMyAdmin or MySQL client) and insert the following content in a single line: ```
  • Position: in
  • File format: mp3
``` 2. Go to Shop **Parameters > Search > Search** and click **Re-build the entire index**. 3. In phpMyAdmin or MySQL client, run: ```sql SELECT * FROM `ps_search_word` WHERE `word` LIKE 'infile'; ``` 4. Confirm that the incorrect word infile has been indexed instead of the two correct tokens `in` and `file`. ### PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened 9.0.0 ### How you installed PrestaShop _No response_ ### PHP version(s) where the bug happened _No response_ ### If your bug is related to a module, specify its name and its version _No response_ ### Your company or customer's name goes here (if applicable). Codencode snc

title: Fix: Module Development and Distribution: Prestashop deletes automatically src/Entity/index.php, but it does not recursively in subfolders
issue_title: Module Development and Distribution: Prestashop deletes automatically src/Entity/index.php, but it does not recursively in subfolders
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20type%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

This issue affects Add-On Marketplace contributors who are starting adapting their modules to the new Symfony 6.4 layer, used by PS 9+.
My module uses many entities and splits them in subfolders.
In order to ship my package I had to go through validation that rejects my module because I needed to remove all the index.php files in Entity's subfolders. 
I think PS should recursively go through all the Entity's subfolders and wipe the encountered index.php files.
Or...change the validation rules for the Entity folder.

### Steps to reproduce

Premise: you must have subfolders in Entity folder.
Create, install and activate a module having index.php in each Entity's subfolder.
Try to access the backoffice.
It will cause a 500 error, silently managed with a redirect to the frontend.

Now remove the index.php files in the Entity folder and subfolders.
Module will be rejected by validation process.


### Expected behavior

Since PS does not delete the index.php files inside Entity subfolders, but only the one in Entity folder,
this will cause a problem during Doctrine entities scan.
I would expect PS deletes all the indexes.php recursively.

### Actual Result

_No response_

9.0.0 and above

download and installed

title: Fix states lookup using row indexes instead of country IDs
issue_title: Carrier::getDeliveredCountries() uses wrong states ID resulting in wrong countries list
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

The new getDeliveredCountries() code has an error when fetching active states linked to delivered countries.
This is because when using the $countries array in `array_keys($countries)` its keys are in numeric order starting from 0, not using id_country as keys.
$countries has no id_country as keys. $result has them.
So `SELECT` is using `IN (0,1,2,3,....)` instead of correct country ids. This results in wrong countries list with countries without carries in it.
https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/25f0ef48696506fcee01e34de069d0c7a3b7c144/classes/Carrier.php#L670

Correct country list with ONLY countries with a carrier enabled.

Just call the Carrier::getDeliveredCountries() function. You'll also get countries for which there aren't carriers available. For better proof, disable carriers for the countries with low states ID in them (like 0,1,2,3,4). They will be included anyway for the error explained in description.

title: Fix:  Changing an order's status throws "Duplicate entry '<idp>-<idpa>-0-0' for product_sqlstock" when the order contains a deleted combination (single-shop)
issue_title: Changing an order's status throws "Duplicate entry '<idp>-<idpa>-0-0' for product_sqlstock" when the order contains a deleted combination (single-shop)
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already searched in existing issues and found no previous report describing this exact reproduction.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

On a **single-shop** install (no multistore, no stock sharing, `share_stock = 0`), changing an order's status fails with:

```
[PrestaShopException code 23000] : SQLSTATE[23000]: Integrity constraint violation: 1062 Duplicate entry '14-183-0-0' for key 'ps_stock_available.product_sqlstock'
```

The error is order-specific: some orders move to the new status fine, others always fail.

**Root cause (investigated):** the failing order contains a **product combination that was later deleted**. `order_detail` still references the old `id_product_attribute` (e.g. `183`), but that combination no longer exists in `product_attribute` / `product_attribute_shop`. When the new status updates stock, `StockManager::getStockAvailableByProduct()` / `StockAvailable::setQuantity()` cannot resolve a shop context for the dead combination and writes a `stock_available` row with `id_shop = 0, id_shop_group = 0`. On a single-shop store this `0-0` row is invalid (it should be `id_shop = 1`). The first qualifying order creates that orphan row; any later order referencing the same deleted combination then collides on the `product_sqlstock` unique key.

Still present (verified in source) in **8.2.6** and **9.1.3**: in `src/Adapter/StockManager::getStockAvailableByProduct()`, when `$id_shop === null` and stock is not shared, `$stockAvailable->id_shop = (int) $id_shop;` evaluates to `0`.

### Expected behavior

Changing an order's status should not fail when an order line references a combination that has since been deleted. A `stock_available` row should never be written with `id_shop = 0` on a single-shop install.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Single-shop install (no multistore).
2. Create a product with a combination (e.g. weight "100 g") → `id_product_attribute = A`.
3. Place an order containing that combination (`order_detail.product_attribute_id = A`).
4. Delete combination `A` from the product (e.g. replace it with another weight).
5. Set that order to a status that updates stock (e.g. "Delivered"). → A `stock_available` row `(product, A, 0, 0)` gets created; this order succeeds.
6. Set another order that also contains combination `A` to that status. → `Duplicate entry '<product>-A-0-0' for key 'product_sqlstock'`.

8.2.1 (code path unchanged through 8.2.6 and 9.1.3)

title: Fix "Array to string conversion" in RenderedHook::outputContent()
issue_title: Array to string conversion in RenderedHook::outputContent() when legacy modules return hook content
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20type%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

A PHP E_WARNING "Array to string conversion" is triggered on every admin page
  that renders a legacy module hook through the Symfony hook dispatcher.

  The warning originates in RenderedHook::outputContent() (line 55) which calls
  implode('', $this->content) expecting string values, but receives arrays.
  This is caused by LegacyHookSubscriber wrapping hook output in a single-element
  array via setContent([content], listener), while HookDispatcher stores the
  result of popContent() — an array — directly into $renderingContent without
  flattening it first.

  In a default PHP setup the warning is silent and "Array" may appear somewhere
  in the rendered HTML (invisible to the user). With any strict error handler
  that converts E_WARNING to exceptions (e.g. a Sentry/monitoring module),
  the admin page crashes entirely.


`E_WARNING: Array to string conversion
  in .../src/Core/Hook/RenderedHook.php on line 55

  #0 [internal]: implode
  #1 .../src/Core/Hook/RenderedHook.php(55): RenderedHook::outputContent
  #2 .../src/PrestaShopBundle/Twig/HookExtension.php(150): HookExtension::renderHook
  #3 .../var/cache/prod/admin/twig/b4/b482833f...php(188): doDisplay
  #4 .../vendor/twig/twig/src/Template.php(402): Twig\Template::yield
  #5 .../vendor/twig/twig/src/Template.php(358): Twig\Template::display
  #6 .../vendor/twig/twig/src/Template.php(373): Twig\Template::render
  #7 .../vendor/symfony/ux-twig-component/src/ComponentRenderer.php(77)
  #8 .../vendor/symfony/ux-twig-component/src/ComponentRenderer.php(56)
  #9 .../vendor/symfony/ux-twig-component/src/Twig/ComponentRuntime.php(51)
  ...
  #N .../src/PrestaShopBundle/Controller/Admin/Improve/ModuleController.php(91)`

### Steps to reproduce

Note: this warning is silently swallowed by PHP's default handler —
  implode() substitutes "Array" for the array value and execution continues.
  The issue only surfaces as a hard crash when a strict error handler is active
  (e.g. a Sentry monitoring module). The steps below include a temporary
  snippet to make the warning visible without any third-party module.

  1. Add the following temporary error handler at the top of config/config.inc.php
     (remove it after reproduction):

       set_error_handler(function (int $errno, string $errstr, string $errfile, int $errline): bool {
           if ($errno === E_WARNING && str_contains($errfile, 'RenderedHook.php')) {
               throw new ErrorException($errstr, 0, $errno, $errfile, $errline);
           }
           return false;
       });

  2. Log in to the back-office.

  3. Navigate to Modules > Module Manager.

  4. An ErrorException "Array to string conversion" is thrown,
     visible in the browser (with debug mode on) or in the PHP error log.

  5. Remove the temporary handler from config/config.inc.php.

  ---

  Without step 1, the warning is invisible in the browser. It is only
  observable via a monitoring tool that captures all E_WARNING events
  (confirmed with a Sentry integration module on PS 9.1.3).

### Expected behavior

The hook content returned by legacy modules should render correctly as a
  string in the admin page, with no PHP warning emitted.

  RenderedHook::outputContent() is documented to hold string values
  (['module_name' => 'rendered_content', ...]) and implode() should
  concatenate them without error.

### Actual Result

A PHP E_WARNING "Array to string conversion" is thrown inside
  RenderedHook::outputContent() at line 55 when implode() processes
  $this->content, because each value is an array instead of a string.

  This happens because LegacyHookSubscriber wraps the hook output in a
  single-element array via setContent([content], listener), and
  HookDispatcher stores the result of popContent() — which returns that
  array as-is — directly into $renderingContent without flattening it.

  The mismatch between what LegacyHookSubscriber produces and what
  RenderedHook::outputContent() expects causes the warning on every admin
  page that triggers a rendering hook from a legacy module.

  In a default PHP setup the warning is silent: implode() substitutes
  "Array" for each array value and execution continues, potentially
  corrupting hook output. With a strict error handler (e.g. a Sentry
  monitoring module), the warning is promoted to an exception and the
  admin page crashes entirely.

### PrestaShop version where the bug happens

9.1.3

### How have you installed PrestaShop

_No response_

### PHP version(s) where the bug happened

8.1.34

title: Fix states grid not refreshing after toggle when filters are active
issue_title: States grid list not updated after toggling status when filters are active
issue_body:
## Describe the bug and add attachments

On the migrated Symfony States listing page, when a filter is active (e.g. **Enabled = Yes**) and the user toggles a row's status to **No** via the switch column, the row **stays visible** in the filtered list instead of disappearing.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Go to **International > Location > Tab States** in the back office.
2. In the **Enabled** filter column, select **Yes** and click **Search**.
3. The list now shows only enabled states.
4. On any row, click the toggle switch to disable that state.
5. Observe: the row remains in the list even though it no longer matches the active filter.

## Expected behavior

After toggling the status, the grid should refresh and re-apply the active filters. The toggled row should disappear from the list, exactly as the Zone grid behaves.

## Actual Result

The row stays visible in the filtered list. The status IS correctly updated in the database (the AJAX call succeeds), but no page reload occurs so the grid does not re-apply the filters.

## Root cause (developer note)

Same root cause as #41615 (Countries): `StateController::toggleStatusAction` returns a `JsonResponse` (consumed via AJAX by `AsyncToggleColumnExtension`) without reloading the page. The Zone grid uses `ColumnTogglingExtension` + `RedirectResponse` from the controller, which triggers a full page reload that re-applies active filters.

Fix: change `StateController::toggleStatusAction` to return a `RedirectResponse` with a flash message, and replace `AsyncToggleColumnExtension` with `ColumnTogglingExtension` in `admin-dev/themes/new-theme/js/pages/state/index.ts`.

## PrestaShop version where the bug happens

9.2.0 (develop)

## How have you installed PrestaShop

git clone

## PHP version(s) where the bug happened

8.3.6

## Your company or customer's name goes here (if applicable).

PrestaShop SA

issue_title: Countries grid list not updated after toggling status when filters are active
issue_body:
## Describe the bug and add attachments

On the migrated Symfony Countries listing page, when a filter is active (e.g. **Enabled = Yes**) and the user toggles a row's status to **No** via the switch column, the row **stays visible** in the filtered list instead of disappearing.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Go to **International > Locations > Tab Countries** in the back office.
2. In the **Enabled** filter column, select **Yes** and click **Search**.
3. The list now shows only enabled countries.
4. On any row, click the toggle switch to disable that country.
5. Observe: the row remains in the list even though it no longer matches the active filter.

## Expected behavior

After toggling the status, the grid should refresh and re-apply the active filters. The toggled row should disappear from the list (since it no longer matches the **Enabled = Yes** filter), exactly as the Zones grid behaves.

## Actual Result

The row stays visible in the filtered list after the toggle. The status IS correctly updated in the database (the AJAX call succeeds), but no page reload occurs so the grid does not re-apply the filters.

## Root cause (developer note)

Two mismatched pieces compared to the Zone grid:

1. **JS** — the Country grid uses `AsyncToggleColumnExtension`, which makes an AJAX POST and only updates the toggle button UI without reloading the page. The Zone grid uses `ColumnTogglingExtension`, which submits a standard HTML form POST and triggers a full page reload that re-applies active filters.

2. **PHP** — `CountryController::toggleStatusAction` returns a `JsonResponse`. When `ColumnTogglingExtension` follows the form POST, the browser navigates to the toggle URL and displays the raw JSON instead of being redirected back. The Zone controller returns a `RedirectResponse` with a flash message instead.

Fix: replace `AsyncToggleColumnExtension` with `ColumnTogglingExtension` in `admin-dev/themes/new-theme/js/pages/country/index.ts`, **and** change `CountryController::toggleStatusAction` to return a `RedirectResponse` with a flash message (removing the unused `JsonResponse` import).

## PrestaShop version where the bug happens

9.2.0 (develop)

git clone

8.3.6

title: Cart rule compatibility search does not filter results for new cart rule
issue_title: Cart rule compatibility search does not filter results for new cart rules
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20type%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

In the Back Office, when editing the "Compatible with other cart rules" autocomplete (Catalog → Discounts → new cart rule → Conditions tab → "Compatibility with other cart rules"), typing a term in the search field does not filter the list. All cart rules are returned regardless of what is typed.

This happens whenever the cart rule has no compatibility restriction set yet, i.e.:

when creating a new cart rule (the AJAX call uses id_cart_rule=0), or
when editing an existing cart rule whose cart_rule_restriction = 0.
Root cause is in CartRule::getAssociatedRestrictions() (classes/CartRule.php). When !Validate::isLoadedObject($this) || $this->{$type.'_restriction'} == 0, the method runs an SQL query that never uses the $search_cart_rule_name argument. The LIKE filter on the name only exists in the other branch, reached through getCartRuleCombinations(), which only applies to an already-saved rule with cart_rule_restriction = 1.

Example AJAX request where the search parameter is ignored:

index.php?controller=AdminCartRules&token=...&ajax=1&id_cart_rule=0&action=loadCartRules&limit=40&count=0&type=selected&search=10


### Steps to reproduce

1. Go to Catalog → Discounts and create several cart rules with distinct names (e.g. 10% off, -50% summer, Free shipping).
2. Click Add new cart rule and open the Conditions tab.
3. In "Compatibility with other cart rules", type part of a name in the search field (e.g. 10).
4. Observe the suggestions list.

### Expected behavior

The list is filtered to only the cart rules whose name matches the typed term.

### Actual Result

The search term is ignored: the full list of cart rules is returned (e.g. -50% summer and Free shipping still appear when searching for 10).

8.x.x - 9.x.x

title: Fix: Multishop: cache_default_attribute is not reset for all shops when changing a product with combinations to a standard product

issue_body:

### Describe the bug and add attachments

In a multishop context, when a product has combinations, PrestaShop stores the default combination ID in the `cache_default_attribute` field of the `product_shop` table.

If the product type is later changed from a product with combinations to **Standard product**, the `cache_default_attribute` value is reset to `0` only for the default shop.

1. Enable multishop.

title: Guard product page when product is null
issue_title: Invalid product URLs trigger Fatal in ProductController::assignPriceAndTax (PHP 8 / PS 9)
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20type%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

`ProductController::initContent()` unconditionally calls `assignPriceAndTax()` without checking whether `$this->product` is a loaded object. When the product cannot be loaded (deleted, inactive, invalid id in the URL), `init()` already
 handled the case by setting the 404 template and returning , but `Controller::run()` keeps going and calls `initContent()` anyway, leading to a Fatal error.

**Call chain:**
```
Controller::run() [classes/controller/Controller.php:308]
  → ProductController::initContent() [controllers/front/ProductController.php:306]
    → ProductController::assignPriceAndTax() [line 529]
       → crash on line 536 (getTaxesRate on null) OR line 539 (getPriceStatic with null id)
```

**Two observable crash points:**

- `ProductController.php:536` , `$this->product->getTaxesRate(...)` → Fatal `Call to a member function getTaxesRate() on null` when `$this->product === null` (URL has `id_product=0` or missing id).
- `ProductController.php:539` , `Product::getPriceStatic($this->product->id, ...)` → `PrestaShopException('Product ID is invalid.')` when `$this->product` is a non-loaded Product object (`new Product(XXXXX)` where the id doesn't exist
returns an object with `id = null`).

**Why `init()` doesn't prevent it:** `init()` correctly detects the invalid product (line 133) and calls `setTemplate('errors/404'); return;`, but the `return` only exits `init()`, not `run()`. `Controller::run()` proceeds to call
`initContent()` regardless.

**Why this is a PHP 8 regression:** PS 1.7 / PS 8 `ProductController` had the same logical flaw, but PHP 7 tolerated `null->method()` with a silent warning. PHP 8 turns it into a `TypeError`.

**Real-world impact:** on any production store with indexed URLs, search engine crawlers (Google, Bing, Facebook) continuously hit URLs of deleted/renamed products. On our store (540k orders, 50k+ products, multilingual) this produces
~40 `*ERROR* Product ID is invalid` entries per hour in `var/logs/<YYYYMMDD>_exception.log`, plus occasional 500s in Apache error log. Zero functional impact (caught exceptions are silenced upstream for most code paths), but the log
noise drowns out legitimate errors.

### Proposed fix options

1. **Guard at the top of `assignPriceAndTax()`:**
   ```php
   protected function assignPriceAndTax(): void
   {
       if (!Validate::isLoadedObject($this->product)) {
           return;
       }
       // ... existing code ...
   }
   ```
2. **Guard at the top of `initContent()`** , protects all `assign*` helpers (`assignCategory`, `assignAttributesCombinations`, etc.) which have the same latent issue.
3. **Abort the run flow in `Controller::run()`** when a 404 template was already set by `init()`. Most invasive, but fixes the class of bugs globally (`CategoryController::getCategoryToRedirectTo()` has the same pattern, crashing on
orphaned inactive categories).

Option 2 is the cleanest local fix.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On any PS 9 install, hit a URL of a non-existent or deleted product, e.g.:
   ```
   https://<shop>/<lang>/999999-nonexistent.html
   https://<shop>/<lang>/<id_of_deleted_product>-<old-slug>.html
   ```
2. Browser receives `HTTP 500`.
3. Check `var/logs/<YYYYMMDD>_exception.log` and `/var/log/apache2/error.log`:
   - `PHP Fatal error: Uncaught Error: Call to a member function getTaxesRate() on null in controllers/front/ProductController.php:536`
   - And/or `*ERROR* Product ID is invalid. at line 3363 in file classes/Product.php`
4. Stack trace consistently terminates at `ProductController::assignPriceAndTax()` → `initContent()` → `Controller::run()`.

### Expected behavior

A request to a non-existent or deleted product URL should return HTTP 404 rendered via the `errors/404` template that `init()` already selected, with no Fatal error, no PrestaShopException, and no entry in `exception.log`.

### Actual Result

HTTP 500 (or silent caught exception), every hit produces at least one log entry. On a shop with crawler traffic, `exception.log` accumulates thousands per day.

### PrestaShop version where the bug happens

9.1.0, 8.2.5

### How have you installed PrestaShop

_No response_

### PHP version(s) where the bug happened

8.1

title: Fix attribute and attribute group position ordering in core methods
issue_title: Attribute swatches on homepage ignore position ordering
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20type%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

When reordering attributes in **Catalog > Attributes & Features** (e.g. moving "Black" before "White" in the Colour group), the configured position is respected on the product detail page but ignored in other places like the homepage featured products.

The product detail page correctly sorts attributes by position, but other methods like `getAttributeCombinations()`, `getAttributeCombinationsById()`, `getAttributesResume()` and `getAttributesInformationsByProduct()` sort by `id_product_attribute` (creation order) or have no ORDER BY at all.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Go to **Catalog > Attributes & Features > Colour**
2. Reorder so that **Black** is before **White** (drag Black above White, or edit positions)
3. Go to the **product detail page** for "Hummingbird printed t-shirt"
4. **Observe:** Colour swatches show Black before White ✅ (correct)
5. Go back to the **homepage** → "Popular Products" section (`ps_featuredproducts`)
6. **Observe:** The same product's colour swatches show White before Black ❌ (wrong — ignores position)
7. Go to **Clothes > Men** category page
8. **Observe:** Colour swatches under product names are also in wrong order ❌

### Expected behavior

Attribute ordering should be consistent everywhere and respect the position configured in the back office.

title: Fix: CountryQueryBuilder::getCountQueryBuilder() always returns 1 instead of the true total
issue_title: CountryQueryBuilder::getCountQueryBuilder() always returns 1 instead of the true total
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20type%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

`CountryQueryBuilder::getCountQueryBuilder()` always returns `1` as the country count, regardless of how many countries exist in the database.

The root cause is that `->groupBy('c.id_country')` is placed in the shared `getQueryBuilder()` method (`src/Core/Grid/Query/CountryQueryBuilder.php`, line 106), which is called by **both** `getSearchQueryBuilder()` and `getCountQueryBuilder()`. The count query therefore inherits `GROUP BY`, becoming:

```sql
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.id_country)
FROM ps_country c
INNER JOIN ps_country_lang cl ON cl.id_country = c.id_country AND cl.id_lang = 1
INNER JOIN ps_zone z ON z.id_zone = c.id_zone
INNER JOIN ps_country_shop cs ON c.id_country = cs.id_country AND cs.id_shop IN (1)
GROUP BY c.id_country;
```

This returns one row per country, each with value `1`. `DoctrineGridDataFactory::fetchOne()` picks the first row → the total is always `1`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install PrestaShop with the default country dataset.
2. Run the following SQL against your database (replace `id_lang` and `id_shop` with your actual values):

```sql
-- Find your values:
SELECT id_lang FROM ps_lang WHERE active = 1 LIMIT 1;
SELECT id_shop FROM ps_shop WHERE active = 1 LIMIT 1;

-- Buggy count query (as generated by getCountQueryBuilder):
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.id_country)
FROM ps_country c
INNER JOIN ps_country_lang cl ON cl.id_country = c.id_country AND cl.id_lang = 1
INNER JOIN ps_zone z ON z.id_zone = c.id_zone
INNER JOIN ps_country_shop cs ON c.id_country = cs.id_country AND cs.id_shop IN (1)
GROUP BY c.id_country;
```

3. Observe that the query returns **241 rows, each containing `1`**, instead of a single row with `241`.
4. Confirm by inspecting `CountryQueryBuilder::getCountQueryBuilder()` in `src/Core/Grid/Query/CountryQueryBuilder.php` — `groupBy('c.id_country')` is inherited from `getQueryBuilder()`.

### Expected behavior

`getCountQueryBuilder()` should return a single row with the true total number of countries (e.g. `241`), so that any consumer of `DoctrineGridDataFactory` with the country grid receives the correct `totalItems`.

### Actual Result

_No response_

### PrestaShop version where the bug happens

9.1.x

git clone

8.1

title: Fix pass shop group ID when setting context in LogoUploader
issue_title: Uploading logo in Design -> Theme & Logo in multistore with a single shop selected causes TypeError with PHP 8.3
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

Updating a logo, mail logo or invoice in multistore with single shop selected causes TypeError with PHP 8.3 and crashes. 

**TypeError**
_ShopCore::getGroupIdFromShopId(): Argument #1 ($shopId) must be of type int, null given, called in ../prestashop/classes/shop/Shop.php on line 1015_

This issue also causes **ShopException** _Shop group id 0 is invalid. Shop group id must be a number that is greater than zero._



Culprit is `\PrestaShop\PrestaShop\Core\Shop\LogoUploader::updateInMultiShopContext`  that calls `Shop::setContext(Shop::CONTEXT_SHOP);` without `$idShop` as second argument even though it is readily available. Without `$idShop` `\ShopCore::setContext` tries to call `Shop::getGroupIdFromShopId($id)` with $id value of null and getGroupIdFromShopId is defined with typehint int.
I searched the project and luckily didn't find any other invalid calls to `Shop::setContext(Shop::CONTEXT_SHOP);` without Shop ID so just adding idShop as argument should be enough.

`\PrestaShop\PrestaShop\Core\Shop\LogoUploader::updateInMultiShopContext` also makes couple of calls `Shop::setContext(Shop::CONTEXT_GROUP);` without second `$id` argument that is also available in the same function. Therefore that is probably not working as intended and might cause some issues, but I didn't get in that deep.


### Expected behavior

Uploading theme logo would change the logo.

### Steps to reproduce

In multistore with a single shop selected
1. Open Design -> Theme & Logo
2. Check Header logo
3. Add logo file 
4. Click Save

9.0.2

title: Fix: Bug: reserved_quantity not updated when "Share available quantities for sale" is enabled (Multishop)
issue_title: Bug: reserved_quantity not updated when "Share available quantities for sale" is enabled (Multishop)
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20type%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

In a multishop environment with 2 shops in the same shop group, when the option:

**Shop Group → Share available quantities for sale**

is enabled (`true`),

product quantities are shared between shops.

However, when placing an order, the system does not correctly update the `reserved_quantity` field in the `stock_available` table.

This happens because in this situation, the `stock_available` records have `id_shop = 0`, but the `PrestaShop\PrestaShop\Adapter::updateReservedProductQuantity()` method performs the update by passing `id_shop = ID_SHOP` (e.g., `id_shop = 1`). Therefore, the query does not match any row in stock_available.

As a result, `reserved_quantity` is never updated.

When the order status changes to **Shipped**: `physical_quantity` is never recalculated correctly.

### Steps to reproduce

- Enable multishop.
- Create a shop group with:
  - 2 shops
  - "Share available quantities for sale" = true
-  Create a product with stock.
- Place an order in one shop.
-  Check the `stock_available` table and verify that the `reserved_quantity` field has not changed (it remains 0), while it should be updated with the purchased quantity.

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20type%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

When fuzzy search is enabled and the nearest word contains an apostrophe (e.g. s'u), Search::find builds SQL like:
... sw.word LIKE 's'u'
This causes SQL syntax error 1064 and returns 500.

Proposed fix:
In classes/Search.php, when fuzzy search returns closestWord, pass it through getSearchParamFromWord() to escape it properly:

$closestWord = static::findClosestWeightestWord($context, $word);
if ($closestWord) {
    $sql_param_search = self::getSearchParamFromWord($closestWord);
}

This prevents SQL like ... LIKE 's'u'.

### Steps to reproduce

1) PrestaShop 9.x, fuzzy search enabled (PS_SEARCH_FUZZY = 1).
2) Ensure ps_search_word contains a word with apostrophe (e.g. from product name “s'u”).
3) Search for a term with no direct matches (e.g. “shu”) to trigger fuzzy search.
4) Observe 500 and SQL error 1064 near "u'".


### Expected behavior

Search should return empty results without SQL error.


### Actual Result

SQL syntax error 1064.


### PrestaShop version where the bug happens

9.0.2

### How have you installed PrestaShop

downloading from prestashop site

8.2.4

title: Fix getting specific price for a given customer group
issue_title: Cart > getSpecificPrice called with shop group id rather than customer group id
issue_body:
**Describe the bug**
In the cart, reduction is shown in amount instead of percentage.

Debugging, I suspect the bug is due to the line 585 in classes/Cart.php :
`SpecificPrice::getSpecificPrice( ... (6 parameters), $this->id_shop_group, ...)`
But looking at the definition of this method :
`public static function getSpecificPrice(... (6 parameters), $id_group, ...)`

In other words : the method is asking for a (customer) group id, and a shop_group id is given instead.

(Consequence : 
- no specific price is found
- so reduction_type is set to 0
- so, in the template, the test '== amount' is valuated as true
- so, the reduction is shown in amount
)

**Steps to Reproduce**
I didn't try to reduce the case to a reproductible one, but following steps should be sufficient :

1. start from a default mono-shop installation of Prestashop 1.6.1.24, with only one shop group whose id is 1
2. create a customer group TEST (whose id is > 1)
3. create a customer FOO, and put him in this group
4. for a product BAR, create a specific price (-10%) for this group
5. log in as FOO, add BAR in your cart
6. go to cart
7. expected : the reduction is shown in percentage (as in Prestashop 1.6.0.x)
8. observed : the reduction is shown in amount

This line has been introduced by the following commit :
https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/commit/20b7c28f188560f2ccc243d77aae3b6ce339bd05 − Optimize Cart::getProducts performances & factorize some queries by @jocel1

**Additional infos**

- PrestaShop version: 1.7.6.0
- PHP version: 7.2

issue_body:

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

### Describe the bug and add attachments

When using the product class function getProductName and including the feature id parameter.
it uses this SQL
`$query->select('IFNULL(CONCAT(pl.name, \' : \', GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT agl.`name`, \' - \', al.name SEPARATOR \', \')),pl.name) as name');`

instead of 
`$query->select('IFNULL(CONCAT(pl.name, \' : \', GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT agl.`public_name`, \' - \', al.name SEPARATOR \', \')),pl.name) as name');`

So the name returns the internal name of the group and not the expected public one.

### Expected behavior

The name returned should be using the public values not the internal ones.

### Steps to reproduce

1. go the attribute groups in the BO
2. set different values on name and public name for a group like color.
3. run the code Product::getProductName($id_product, $id_product_attribute, $id_lang); for a product with color, you will get the wrong name.

title: Fix Category::searchByPath losing context during recursion
issue_title: Category::searchByPath loses parent context after creating missing segment
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

When Category::searchByPath() creates a missing category segment via the $objectToCreate callback, the subsequent recursive call loses parent context. This can cause the next lookup to resolve the wrong category when identical names exist under different parents, or prevent correct path traversal.

The method is designed to recurse, but it currently recurses using only the segment name instead of the accumulated path.

Actual behavior
The method recurses using only the current segment name:
Category::searchByPath($idLang, $categoryName);
This drops the accumulated path and parent context.

Root cause
The recursive call uses the segment name instead of the accumulated path (path-so-far), causing loss of $idParentCategory context.



### Expected behavior

After creating a missing path segment, searchByPath() should continue recursion using the full path up to the created segment, preserving parent context for subsequent lookups.

### Steps to reproduce

Create the following categories:

A (under root)

Other/A (same name under a different parent)

Call: Category::searchByPath($idLang, 'Other/A/NewChild', $creatorObject, $creatorMethod);
where NewChild does not exist and is created by the callback.

Observe that after creating NewChild, the recursion can resolve the wrong parent or fail to continue traversal correctly.

issue_body: ### Prerequisites - [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). - [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug. ### Describe the bug and add attachments When trying to use the service `prestashop.core.import.csv_file_reader`, which points to the class `PrestaShop\PrestaShop\Core\Import\File\CsvFileReader`, the following error occurs: `You have requested a non-existent service "session"` A screenshot of the error is attached. ### Additional context This issue does not occur in PrestaShop 8 because the `session` service was still available. issue_body: ### Prerequisites - [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). - [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug. ### Describe the bug and add attachments In the Back Office, on the order detail page (Order totals summary), the **tax/VAT total** is not displayed when the customer group associated with the order (e.g. **Customer**) has the following setting: **Shop parameters > Customer Settings > Groups > Price display method = Tax included** If the same group is instead configured as: **Price display method = Tax excluded** the tax (VAT) summary is correctly displayed. In my opinion, the VAT/tax summary should be **always visible** in the Back Office order view, or at least also visible when the group is set to **Tax included**, since this is an administrative and accounting-relevant value. A **video** and **screenshots** are attached to show the behavior. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da5493c0-6c11-4ccf-8282-6c83639d614f ### Expected behavior _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce 1. Go to **Shop parameters > Customer Settings > Groups** 2. Edit the **Customer** group 3. Set **Price display method** to **Tax included** 4. Open **Order ID 1** 5. Notice that the **VAT/tax summary is not displayed** in the order totals block 6. Go back to **Shop parameters > Customer Settings > Groups** 7. Edit the **Customer** group again 8. Set **Price display method** to **Tax excluded** 9. Open **Order ID 1** again 10. Notice that the **VAT/tax summary is now displayed** ### PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened 9.0.x ### How you installed PrestaShop _No response_ ### PHP version(s) where the bug happened _No response_ ### Your company or customer's name goes here (if applicable). title: Fix: doctrine throws error from the beginning: There is no column with name "theme_name" on table "ps_image_type"
issue_title: doctrine throws error from the beginning: There is no column with name "theme_name" on table "ps_image_type".
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

After a brand new  installation with docker the module-page lists ca. 40 modules which needs upgrade. At least the upgrade of 

> PrestaShop Marketplace in your Back Office
> v5.1.0 -> v5.2.1 

breaks the entire installation.

After investigating with cli-console i found that `doctrine:schema:validate` throws an error - also on a brand new installation:

```
root@7e555091bfb4:/var/www/html# php bin/console doctrine:schema:validate

Mapping
-------


 [OK] The mapping files are correct.


Database
--------

13:33:34 CRITICAL  [console] Error thrown while running command "doctrine:schema:validate". Message: "There is no column with name "theme_name" on table "ps_image_type"." ["exception" => Doctrine\DBAL\Schema\Exception\ColumnDoesNotExist^ { …},"command" => "doctrine:schema:validate","message" => "There is no column with name "theme_name" on table "ps_image_type"."]

In ColumnDoesNotExist.php line 16:

  There is no column with name "theme_name" on table "ps_image_type".


doctrine:schema:validate [--em EM] [--skip-mapping] [--skip-sync] [--skip-property-types]
```

My speculation is that the `schema-update` fails while upgrading the module and therefore leaves the entire installation in an unusable state.

### Expected behavior

To upgrade modules without any errors occuring.

### Steps to reproduce

1. install prestashop according to the [guidelines](https://devdocs.prestashop-project.org/9/basics/installation/environments/docker/)
2. login to admin backend
3. navigate to module management
4. click 'upgrade' next to module 'PrestaShop Marketplace in your Back Office'

an error occurs and on page-reload the installation answers with 500 internal server error.

### PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened

9.0.1

### How you installed PrestaShop

docker

8.4.12 (docker)

title: Fix some type issues related to carriers
issue_title: TypeError in Carrier repositories on PrestaShop 9 (string returned instead of int)
issue_body:
**Prerequisites**

-  I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

-  I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

**Describe the bug**

- While testing PrestaShop 9.0.1, I encountered blocking TypeError exceptions when editing or saving a carrier in the Back Office.

- This is caused by strict typing enforcement (declare(strict_types=1) with Symfony 6), where some values retrieved from the database are strings, but the repository methods explicitly expect int.

- This results in fatal errors that make the carrier management section unusable.

**Error 1 – Editing a carrier**

`TypeError: PrestaShop\PrestaShop\Adapter\Carrier\Repository\CarrierRepository::getOrdersCount(): 
Return value must be of type int, string returned
`

Root cause: `fetchOne()` returns a string for `COUNT(*)`, but the method has a strict `int ` return type.

**Error 2 – Saving a carrier**

`TypeError: CarrierRangeRepository::getRangeMethodTable(): 
Argument #1 ($calculatingMethod) must be of type int, string given
`

Root cause: `$carrier->shipping_method` is retrieved as a string from the database, but
`getRangeMethodTable(int $calculatingMethod)` expects an integer.

**Affected files:**

- `src/Adapter/Carrier/Repository/CarrierRepository.php`
- `src/Adapter/Carrier/Repository/CarrierRangeRepository.php`

**Expected behavior**

- Editing and saving a carrier should work without triggering fatal errors.
- Carrier repositories should properly handle typing (casting values or enforcing correct hydration types).

**Temporary workaround**

Explicit casts added in repositories during testing:

`return (int) $count;
$this->getRangeMethodTable((int) $carrier->shipping_method);
`

This restores Back Office functionality.
A core-level fix for proper type handling or entity hydration is preferable long-term.

**Steps to reproduce**

- Install PrestaShop 9.0.1 (clean installation).
- Go to Back Office → Improve → Shipping → Carriers.
- Create a new carrier or edit an existing one.
- Click Save or open the carrier edit page.
- Observe TypeError and HTTP 500 page.

**PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened**

- 9.0.1

**How you installed PrestaShop**

- Official PrestaShop GitHub package
- Manual installation on a test environment
- No third-party distribution or overrides

**PHP version(s) where the bug happened**

- PHP 8.3.28

**Module related**

- Not related to any module
- Occurs on core carrier management only

**Proposed patch / fix**

1 - Fix `CarrierRepository::getOrdersCount()`

`- return $count;
+ return (int) $count;
`

2 - Fix `CarrierRangeRepository::getRangeMethodTable()` calls

`- $rangeTable = $this->getRangeMethodTable($carrier->shipping_method);
+ $rangeTable = $this->getRangeMethodTable((int) $carrier->shipping_method);
`

**Rationale:**

- `fetchOne()` returns a string even for `COUNT(*)`
- `$carrier->shipping_method` is hydrated as string from DB
- Strict typing in Symfony 6 + `declare(strict_types=1)` triggers fatal errors
- Explicit casts fix the immediate TypeError without altering behavior

**Status:**

✔️ Fix tested
✔️ Restores carrier edit/save in Back Office
⚠️ Temporary workaround pending core-level typing normalization

**Anticipation of the question: “Why not fix hydration instead?”**

Fixing hydration at the source is the ideal long-term solution.

However, this patch stays minimal and non-invasive because:

1. **Hydration changes have a wide impact**

- Carrier entities are legacy-driven and hydrated from multiple layers (Doctrine DBAL, legacy ObjectModel, repositories)
- Changing hydration globally would require auditing all read/write paths and validating module compatibility

2. **Strict typing causes immediate failures**

- Symfony 6 + `declare(strict_types=1)` now fails at runtime for previously tolerated values
- Explicit casts address the immediate TypeError without changing the data model

3. **Doctrine DBAL behavior is expected**

- `fetchOne()` returns strings even for COUNT(*)
- Repository-level cast

**Scope and risk management:**

- Fixes a blocking Back Office error
- Fully backward-compatible
- Limited to exact failure points
- Does not change public APIs or entity definitions

This patch is intended as a safe, targeted fix for PS 9.x, while allowing future core-level typing normalization.

**Here is a complete diff ready to submit on GitHub to fix the TypeErrors in carrier repositories on PrestaShop 9. It corresponds to the issue description and the temporary patch you tested :**

```
`Fix CarrierRepository::getOrdersCount()

File: src/Adapter/Carrier/Repository/CarrierRepository.php

diff --git a/src/Adapter/Carrier/Repository/CarrierRepository.php b/src/Adapter/Carrier/Repository/CarrierRepository.php
index XXXXXXX..YYYYYYY 100644
--- a/src/Adapter/Carrier/Repository/CarrierRepository.php
+++ b/src/Adapter/Carrier/Repository/CarrierRepository.php
@@ -335,7 +335,7 @@ class CarrierRepository
         $count = $this->connection
             ->createQueryBuilder()
             ->select('COUNT(oc.id_order)')
             ->from($this->dbPrefix . 'orders', 'oc')
             ->where('oc.id_carrier = :carrierId')
             ->setParameter('carrierId', $carrierId->getValue())
             ->executeQuery()
             ->fetchOne();
-        return $count;
+        return (int) $count;
     }

Fix CarrierRangeRepository::getRangeMethodTable() calls

File: src/Adapter/Carrier/Repository/CarrierRangeRepository.php

Method set()
diff --git a/src/Adapter/Carrier/Repository/CarrierRangeRepository.php b/src/Adapter/Carrier/Repository/CarrierRangeRepository.php
index 2345678..bcdef01 100644
--- a/src/Adapter/Carrier/Repository/CarrierRangeRepository.php
+++ b/src/Adapter/Carrier/Repository/CarrierRangeRepository.php
@@ -81,7 +81,7 @@ class CarrierRangeRepository
         // Get carrier
         $carrier = $this->carrierRepository->get($carrierId);
-        $rangeTable = $this->getRangeMethodTable($carrier->shipping_method);
+        $rangeTable = $this->getRangeMethodTable((int) $carrier->shipping_method);

Method applyRangeTypeForQuery()
@@ -188,7 +188,7 @@ class CarrierRangeRepository
     private function applyRangeTypeForQuery(QueryBuilder $queryBuilder, Carrier $carrier): QueryBuilder
     {
         // Define which table to join based on carrier shipping method
-        $tableRange = $this->getRangeMethodTable($carrier->shipping_method);
+        $tableRange = $this->getRangeMethodTable((int) $carrier->shipping_method);

         // Join the range table and order by range
         $queryBuilder->innerJoin(
             'cd',
             $this->dbPrefix . $tableRange,
             'cr',
             'cd.id_' . $tableRange . ' = cr.id_' . $tableRange . ' AND cr.id_carrier = :carrierId'
         )
             ->orderBy('cr.id_' . $tableRange, 'ASC');

         return $queryBuilder;
     }
`

```
**Rationale / explanation for GitHub (to paste in the PR or issue body) :**

- fetchOne() always returns a string, even for COUNT(*) → explicit (int) cast ensures the strict return type is respected.
- $carrier->shipping_method is retrieved as a string from the database → cast to (int) before using it in getRangeMethodTable(int $calculatingMethod).
- Fixes fatal TypeErrors with Symfony 6 + declare(strict_types=1).
- Minimal, non-invasive patch, fully backward-compatible.
- Temporary solution: a full hydration fix would be cleaner but much more impactful.

title: Fix: PHP Fatal error when deleting product image by Webservice API #39111
issue_title: PHP Fatal error when deleting product image by Webservice API
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

There is PHP Fatal error when you try to delete product image by webservice API in Prestashop 9.0.0

I have the following code:

$apiUrl = 'http://localhost/prestashop900/api/images/products/22/32';
$apiKey = 'YOUR_API_KEY';

$ch = curl_init();
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_URL, $apiUrl);
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST, 'DELETE');
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, true);
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_USERPWD, $apiKey . ':');
$response = curl_exec($ch);

After executing this code, the image with ID=32 that belongs to product with ID=22 gets deleted, but there is the following fatal error logged in the server error logs:

PHP Fatal error:  Uncaught Error: Call to a member function get() on null in /www/prestashop900/classes/Image.php:930
Stack trace:
/www/prestashop900/classes/Image.php(642): ImageCore->deleteAutoGeneratedImage(Array, 'jpg', Array)
/www/prestashop900/classes/Image.php(206): ImageCore->deleteImage()
/www/prestashop900/classes/webservice/WebserviceSpecificManagementImages.php(822): ImageCore->delete()

Cause: SymfonyContainer::getInstance() returns null in deleteAutoGeneratedImage() function of Image.php class when running webservice.

### Expected behavior

There should not be fatal error.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Get Webservice key from your Prestashop 9.0.0
2. Copy my code that was given in the issue text.
3. Replace shop URL and API key.
4. Replace product ID and Image ID with existing ones from your shop.
5. Execute the code.
6. Check server error logs.

9.0.0

title: Fix: Issue retrieving product price when adding the first specific_price
issue_title: Issue retrieving product price when adding the first specific_price
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

When a new **specific_price** is added and no other specific prices exist in the catalog, the product price retrieved inside the `hookActionObjectSpecificPriceAddAfter` hook does not take the newly added discount into account.

This happens because the configuration `PS_SPECIFIC_PRICE_FEATURE_ACTIVE` is set to 1 only after the specific_price is created. However, the `hookActionObjectSpecificPriceAddAfterhook` is executed before this configuration is updated.
As a result, when the hook attempts to retrieve the product price, the feature is still disabled (`NULL`) and the discount is not applied.

### Expected behavior

The price retrieved inside the hook should correctly reflect the newly added specific_price, even when it is the first specific_price in the catalog.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install the module [issue40255.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23959265/issue40255.zip).
2. Ensure that no specific prices exist in the catalog.

title: Fix: Cart rule combinations lost when saving if lazy-loaded list (jscroll) is not fully loaded
issue_title: Cart rule combinations lost when saving if lazy-loaded list (jscroll) is not fully loaded
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

When editing a cart rule with a large number of “compatible cart rules”, the Back Office loads the list using *infinite scroll* (`jscroll`), but **only the currently loaded items are included in the `<select name="cart_rule_select[]>` POST payload**.

Because of this, when saving a cart rule **without scrolling the list to the end**, PrestaShop deletes *all* existing combinations for that rule (as part of the normal `afterUpdate` process), then recreates them only from the partial list sent in the form.

This leads to **data loss**: most combinations disappear permanently after the user saves the rule.

This affects both:

- existing combinations loaded from DB,
- new combinations added via AJAX,
- any combinations not currently loaded in the DOM at save time.

This is a **core data integrity bug** caused by BO lazy-loading in file [conditions.tpl](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/65e40453e0478cf5472093b69ae567d0d2b5d6b4/admin-dev/themes/default/template/controllers/cart_rules/conditions.tpl#L271) + how PrestaShop reconstructs cart rule combinations after update.

### Expected behavior

Saving a cart rule **should not delete combinations that were not visible in the DOM** due to lazy-loading.

Either:

- the UI should send **all existing combination IDs**, not only loaded items,  
**or**
- the backend should preserve existing combinations instead of deleting them blindly.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a large number of cart rules (e.g. 1000+).
2. Edit any cart rule that has many combinable rules.
3. In the “Conditions” tab, the list of combinable rules is rendered using `jscroll` and loads items in batches via AJAX infinite scroll.
4. Do **not** scroll to the bottom — leave most combinations not loaded.
5. Click **Save**.
6. PrestaShop removes all combinations:
   ```sql
   DELETE FROM cart_rule_combination 
   WHERE id_cart_rule_1 = X OR id_cart_rule_2 = X
   ```
7. PrestaShop recreates combinations only from:
   ```
   POST['cart_rule_select[]']
   ```
   — which contains **only the few rules loaded at the top**.
8. The majority of combinations are lost.

8.2.0

title: Always request a non cached result in Order::getIdByCartId
issue_title: Order::getIdByCartId in OrderConfirmationControllerCore fails to query order_id when cached
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

When a payment module redirects to order-confirmation, the `OrderId` is fetched using:
`$this->id_order = Order::getIdByCartId((int) $this->id_cart);` https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/1d97fcde1bf31d522cfbcfde904316da1d9088d6/controllers/front/OrderConfirmationController.php#L83

`Order::getIdByCartId` uses `$result = Db::getInstance()->getValue($sql);`, with the default of getValue being to use cache.
Now, in some clustered environments it's possible that the order is created by one node and the confirmation page is server by another; this seems to cause the `Order::getIdByCartId` to return a cached `false`, causing the confirmation page to do an early redirect, exiting early. https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/1d97fcde1bf31d522cfbcfde904316da1d9088d6/controllers/front/OrderConfirmationController.php#L95

In my experiments, forcing `Order::getIdByCartId` to query a non cached result solves the issue.

### Expected behavior

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce

1. Pay an order with a PSP that confirms the payment via S2S callbacks.
2. If the conditions align you will sometimes get redirected away from the confirmation page

title: BO - Orders : Optimized Countries Choice
issue_title: Performance Issue: Heavy SQL Query in OrderCountriesChoiceProvider Slows Down Orders Grid
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

Describe the Bug:
Instead, on every page load the following query runs—twice—processing ~110,698 rows and taking ~759,248 ms:

sql

SELECT SQL_NO_CACHE DISTINCT c.id_country, cl.`name`
FROM `ps_orders` o
INNER JOIN `ps_address` a
    ON a.id_address = o.id_address_delivery
INNER JOIN `ps_country` c
    ON a.id_country = c.id_country
INNER JOIN `ps_country_lang` cl
    ON (c.`id_country` = cl.`id_country`
        AND cl.`id_lang` = 3)
ORDER BY cl.name ASC
This query is defined at line 83 of
src/Adapter/Form/ChoiceProvider/OrderCountriesChoiceProvider.php.

Because it runs on every refresh—even in a single-country store—the Orders grid is nearly unusable due to the excessive database load.

### Expected behavior

The Orders grid should load quickly. If only one country is in use (e.g. Iran), the OrderCountriesChoiceProvider should simply return that country—without running a full SELECT DISTINCT over ps_orders, ps_address, ps_country and ps_country_lang.

### Steps to reproduce

Enable debug/profiling mode in PrestaShop.

Navigate to Sell → Orders in the Back-Office.

Observe the profiler/log output for SQL queries executed during the page load.

issue_title: Makefile PHP_CONT variable fails for npm commands due to missing shell login
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

**OS on which the bug was detected**:  linux

Currently, in the PrestaShop Docker Makefile, the `PHP_CONT` variable is defined as:

`PHP_CONT = $(DOCKER_COMP) exec prestashop-git runuser -u www-data -g www-data --`


When running asset build commands like `make assets`, we sometimes encounter errors such as:

`./tools/assets/build.sh: line 54: npm: command not found`

### Expected behavior

npm, node, and other tools installed in the container should be available when running Makefile commands, without manually opening an interactive shell.

**Solution:**

Executes **bash -lc** inside the container to ensure a login shell, correctly loading environment variables and PATH.

### Steps to reproduce

1. From host, run make assets (or any other asset build command).
2. Observe the error `npm: command not found`

```php
        // this part is missing from version 9.0

            $emailField->addError($this->translator->trans(

                [],

```
