This happens because there is a bug in CartCore class which is returning shipping cost straight from the external module without checking if taxes are used or not: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/178c3532f3fa88469cef70e27c66d90185217406/classes/Cart.php#L3596 https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/178c3532f3fa88469cef70e27c66d90185217406/classes/Cart.php#L3611 There should be a check if taxes are used and should be added if needed in if clauses in classes/Cart.php#L3596 and classes/Cart.php#L3611 like there is in the end of the method: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/178c3532f3fa88469cef70e27c66d90185217406/classes/Cart.php#L3671 ### Expected behavior Shipping price taxes should persist ### Steps to reproduce 1. Set "Free shipping starts at" for example 20 Eur in Shipping Preferences window; 2. Make sure that external shipping module returns "10" in "getOrderShippingCost" method; 3. Then add products to cart with total cart sum lower than 20 Eur, then increase to higher than 20 Eur and you will see than shipping price losses taxes; (21% VAT in my example) ### PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened 8.1.7 ### How you installed PrestaShop _No response_ ### PHP version(s) where the bug happened _No response_ ### If your bug is related to a module, specify its name and its version _No response_ ### Your company or customer's name goes here (if applicable). _No response_

title: Fix: recoverCart link does not log the user. Stuck to process checkout step 1
issue_title: recoverCart link does not log the user. Stuck to process checkout step 1.
issue_body:
<!--
****************************
DO NOT disclose security issues here, contact security@prestashop.com instead!
****************************
-->

#### Describe the bug

When creating an order from BO, when using the link to go to the payment page the checkout process is at step 1 instead of step 3

#### Expected behavior

When using the link to pay in BO from a new order to recover the cart, the admin user is redirected to checkout step 3

#### Steps to Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Go to order in BO
2. Click on 'Add an order'
3. Select registered customer
4. Add item in cart
5. Click on 'Go to payment page' link
6. Get stuck to first checkout step where you need password


#### Additional information

* PrestaShop version: 1.7.6.7
* PHP version: 7.2

#### Temporary fix
FrontController.php in recoverCart function
After :
``` $this->context->cookie->email = $customer->email;```
Add : 
```$this->context->cookie->registerSession(new CustomerSession());```

Get you to the step 2

title: Add idShop cache value for getLinkRewrite Category and Category CMS
issue_title: Category link cache doesn't take shopId as a parameter
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

While working on a `hreflang` generation module, when generating alternate URL's for products, I noticed that product URL with the default category inside was wrong. While the actual `link_rewrite` of the product with shopId and langId is valid, the category `link_rewrite` was only taking langId into account, as a result, if a category present in multiple shops has a different `link_rewrite` for a same given language, it will never be reflected in the URL.

Example :
2 shops (1 and 2) with only one language being English (1)
A category shared in both shops
`link_rewrite` for shop 1 language 1 - "my-nice-category"
`link_rewrite` for shop 2 language 1 - "my-very-nice-category"

A product shared in both shops
`link_rewrite` for shop 1 language 1 - "my-nice-product"
`link_rewrite` for shop 1 language 1 - "my-very-nice-product"

If we generate the product URL using the `Link` object, in the same HTTP request will give:
Shop 1 language 1 - `https://example.shop/my-nice-category/1-my-nice-product`
Shop 2 language 1 - `https://example.shop/my-nice-category/1-my-very-nice-product`

Cause of this behavior:
```php
    public static function getLinkRewrite($idCategory, $idLang)
    {
        if (!Validate::isUnsignedId($idCategory) || !Validate::isUnsignedId($idLang)) {
            return false;
        }

        if (!isset(self::$_links[$idCategory . '-' . $idLang])) { // < Here, this static cache, ignoring shopId
            self::$_links[$idCategory . '-' . $idLang] = Db::getInstance()->getValue('
			SELECT cl.`link_rewrite`
			FROM `' . _DB_PREFIX_ . 'category_lang` cl
			WHERE `id_lang` = ' . (int) $idLang . '
			' . Shop::addSqlRestrictionOnLang('cl') . '
			AND cl.`id_category` = ' . (int) $idCategory);
        }

        return self::$_links[$idCategory . '-' . $idLang];
    }
```

Note: PR pending

### Expected behavior

Shop 1 language 1 - `https://example.shop/my-nice-category/1-my-nice-product`
Shop 2 language 1 - `https://example.shop/my-very-nice-category/1-my-very-nice-product`

### Steps to reproduce

Any version of Prestashop (Oldest one checked is 1.7)

- Enable multistore
- Create a second store
- Create a category in `All` context, then edit the `URL` to a different one in the context of the second shop
- Create a product in `All` context
- Test the URL generation

### PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened

1.7.X

### PHP version(s) where the bug happened

8.1

### If your bug is related to a module, specify its name and its version

_No response_

title: Save address choice on click

issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

In the purchase funnel, if there is more than one address and the customer chooses the address that is not selected by default, the choice is lost if the customer clicks on the link to enter a different address for the billing process.

Example on a default PrestaShop environment :
1. The client has two delivery addresses and one is selected by default:
![image](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/assets/52157233/dc62830c-829c-4d2f-9174-cb515e98c4bd)

2. The client chooses the other delivery address (and not the one by default):
![image](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/assets/52157233/3f67466e-73f2-4052-97a8-f97452807406)


3. The client then clicks on the linK to add another address ('L'adresse de facturation ') for the billing process:
Then the address by default is once again selected and not the one chosen in the previous step.
![image](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/assets/52157233/b000b87a-a380-45e7-92f2-4b9095851041)





### Expected behavior

The delivery address chosen by the client must be still selected when he wants to enter a different billing address

### Steps to reproduce

    • Enter two delivery addresses or more
    • Put an item in the cart and begin the order process
    • Go to the address part of the purchase funnel
    • Selected another delivery address than the one selected by default
    • Click on the link to enter a different address for the billing process
You’ll see that the delivery address is not the one previously selected.

title: BO : Product Form : Use the correct configuration for the Max Filesize
issue_title: BO-Maximum size for a downloadable product is not respected when uploading file
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

Hello,

In Upload quota i fixed values for both fields:
1. Maximum size for attached files 
2. Maximum size for a downloadable product

When creating a virtual product and allow download option, the file choosen should respect the value fixed for **Maximum size for a downloadable product** or the problem is that the size of file upload takes always the value of **Maximum size for attached files**  and ignore the value  **Maximum size for a downloadable product** 

### Expected behavior

When uploading a file for a virtual product (with download option ON) the size of the file should respect the value set in BO, specifically **Maximum size for a downloadable product** which is responsible for : Define the upload limit for a downloadable product (in megabytes).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Go to BO > Advanced Parameters > Administration >  Upload quota section
2. Set the field Maximum size for attached files : 2
3. Set the field Maximum size for a downloadable product :1
4. Click Save button
5. Go to BO > Catalog > Products > click on **New product** button > choose virtual product > click **Add new product** button
6. Go to **virtual product** tab > switch Add downloadable file to **yes**
7. Choose a file with size over than 2 Mo > See error message
See attached screenshot:
![image](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/assets/92626242/612e4e44-b721-45dc-ae3c-f12e9f93370f)
9. Choose another file with size over than 1 and  less than2 Mo (1.5 Mo for exp )> Successful update :x:
   (The file chosen should not be accepted since his size is over than 1Mo already fixed in step 3 )
10. Go to FO > create an order with a virtual product >Go to BO and change status for the order to Delivered
11. Back to FO > Download the virtual product from Order details page
12. See error the download is successful althought the file size is over 1Mo

See attached screenvideo :

https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/assets/92626242/a26d8fb0-c907-4a32-b038-0f7b9667040c



### PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened

8.1.0 & 8.0.4 & 1.7.8.9

title: Ensure specific prices are deleted safely on customer deletion by validating passed ID
issue_title: Calling delete() method on an empty instance of Customer object leads to the deletion of all non-customer-restricted specific prices
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

Calling the delete() method on an empty instance of Customer ObjectModel leads to the deletion **of all** the shop's specific prices that are not restricted to any customer (id_customer = 0).
This corresponds to the majority of specific prices in most cases, so this issue is quite annoying and can have dramatic consequences for the shop sales and marketing campaigns if it happens and is not addressed quickly by restoring a backup.

**This issue is present in all versions of PrestaShop.**

### Expected behavior

When calling the delete() method on an instance of Customer object, we should first validate that the passed Customer ID is not empty before processing the deletion of the customer's specific prices.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In the back office, add one or more specific prices (to any product) without specifying a customer restriction (applicable to all customer)
2. Anywhere in the code (e.g., in the initContent of IndexController or in the displayHeader hook of a module), add one of the following line of code : 
```php
(new Customer())->delete();
(new Customer(null))->delete();
(new Customer(0))->delete();
(new Customer('a string'))->delete(); // argument is casted as integer in the method
```
4. Reload the page corresponding to where you put previous code (e.g., the home page in FO)
5. Go back in BO to the product on which you created the specific prices **=> they have been deleted**

title: Fix: Issue with JS and CSS cache clearing in multishop context
issue_title: Issue with JS and CSS cache clearing in multishop context
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

In a multishop environment with at least two stores, when enabling JavaScript or CSS caching (_Advanced Parameters > Performance > CCC (Combine, Compress, and Cache) > Smart cache for JavaScript / Smart cache for CSS_), an issue occurs when clearing the cache.

When the cache is cleared, the system increments the `PS_CCCCSS_VERSION` and `PS_CCCJS_VERSION` configurations based on the selected shop context. However:

- If the operation is performed while selecting a **single shop**, the configurations are correctly updated only for that specific shop.
- If the cache is cleared while selecting "**All stores**", the system updates only the global configurations and not those of individual shops.

As a result, if the cache was previously cleared for a single shop and then cleared again globally, the individual shop’s configurations are not updated. This causes the front-office to use outdated assets, leading to display and loading issues.

### Expected behavior

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable Multishop:
    - Go to Advanced Parameters > Multistore and enable the multishop feature.
    - Create at least two shops.

2. Enable JS and CSS Caching:
    - Navigate to Advanced Parameters > Performance.
    - Under the CCC (Combine, Compress, and Cache) section, enable:
        -  Smart cache for JavaScript
        -  Smart cache for CSS
    - Save the settings.
3. Clear Cache for a Single Shop:
    -  In the multishop selector (top-left of the back office), select a single shop.
    - Go to Advanced Parameters > Performance and click Clear cache.
    - This will update the "PS_CCCJS_VERSION" and "PS_CCCJS_VERSION" values for the selected shop.
4. Clear Cache for All Shops:
    - In the multishop selector, choose "All stores".
    - Go to Advanced Parameters > Performance and click Clear cache again.
    - This updates only the global configurations but does not affect individual shop configurations.
5. Check the Issue in the Front-Office:
    - Visit the front-office of the previously selected single shop.
    - The shop continues to load outdated JavaScript and CSS assets instead of the refreshed ones.

### PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened

8.x.x

title: Fix: [Bug] Missing attributes autoplay, loop, muted, and playsinline in the video tag within Tools::purifyHTML()
issue_title: [Bug] Missing attributes autoplay, loop, muted, and playsinline in the video tag within Tools::purifyHTML()
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

Currently, the `Tools::purifyHTML()` function defines the <video> element with the following allowed attributes:
- src
- type
- width
- height
- poster
- preload
- controls

However, the following attributes are missing:
- autoplay
- loop
- muted
- playsinline

These attributes are essential for the proper functioning of HTML5 videos, especially for:
- Allowing autoplay (necessary for, for example, background videos);
- Enabling loop;
- Ensuring silent autoplay (as required by browsers);
- Enabling inline playback on mobile devices (avoiding the transition to fullscreen).

### Expected behavior

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable the "Use HTMLPurifier Library" option in the PrestaShop back office.
2. In  cms page insert anHTML block containing the following code:
 ```html
<video autoplay="autoplay" loop="loop" muted="muted" playsinline="playsinline">
    <source src="VIDEO_URL" type="video/mp4">
</video>
```
3. Save the content.
4. Observe that the resulting code is "cleaned", with the desired attributes removed:
 ```html
<video>
    <source src="VIDEO_URL" type="video/mp4">
</video>
```

Do you think it would make sense to enable these attributes? I could create a PR regarding this.

Thank you.

title: Fix performance issue linked to HookModuleFilter PR
issue_title: Performance issue on BackOffice with HookModuleFilter
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

#### Initial issue

The issue lies in the method `HookCore::getHookModuleFilter()` introduced int PR https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/37125, where the system attempts to retrieve the service `PrestaShop\PrestaShop\Core\Hook\HookModuleFilter` using the following instruction:

```php
try {
    $hookModuleFilter = $serviceContainer->get(HookModuleFilter::class);
} catch (Exception $e) {
    return null;
}
```

However, in the back office, the system fails to retrieve it and throws the following exception (handled via try/catch, so it’s not visible):

```php
throw new ServiceNotFoundException($id, null, null, [], sprintf('The "%s" service or alias has been removed or inlined when the container was compiled. You should either make it public, or stop using the container directly and use dependency injection instead.', $id));
```

#### Core issue

The `HookModuleFilter` service is not public in BackOficce (in the Symfony container), as such it cannot be retrieved via `container::get` since it's private, and we cannot inject it properly in this case since the service is inside deep inside some legacy code handling hook execution.

So besides the performance cost of this unreachable service called hundreds of times (for each hook), the other problem is that the feature of hook filtering cannot work in the BackOffice because of this (initial tests were mainly centered on the FrontOffice)

### Expected behavior

The service must be made public, the try/catch can then be simplified, if the service is not found in the future an exception should be triggered to identify the problem right away.

### Steps to reproduce

The bug was not seeable by functional QA, so manual tests should validate that the initial behaviour from https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/discussions/37060 still works as expected.

A complementary QA by dev can be made by adding break points in the `HookCore::getHookModuleFilter` to make sure no `ServiceNotFound` exception is triggered anymore, although it there was it would be seen now since the exception is no longer caught and hidden.

### PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened

9.0.x

### PHP version(s) where the bug happened

8.1

title: Fix: Multishop: Deleting and recreating a combination removes the shared reference (new Product Page V2)
issue_title: Multishop: Deleting and recreating a combination removes the shared reference (new Product Page V2)
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

In a multishop setup with two shops (e.g., **B2C** and **B2B**), using the new product page (Product Page v2), if a product has an active combination for both shops, the following behavior occurs:

The product has an active combination with:
**Size**: S
**Reference**: REFERENCE

If I delete this combination from the **B2B** shop and then recreate it, the system reassigns the same combination (keeping the same ID). This behavior is correct and useful.

Issue: During this process, the system removes the value of the **Reference** (reference) field of the combination. Since the **Reference** field is unique across all shops, it should remain unchanged even after deleting and recreating the combination.

In my opinion, the system should preserve the reference value to avoid data loss and ensure proper management of combinations in a multishop context.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa953118-81a5-4c49-b6b3-38bbe4b77241

### Expected behavior

The system should retain the value of the **Reference** (REFERENCE) field.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set up a multishop configuration with at least two shops (e.g., B2C and B2B).
2. Create a product with an active combination shared across both shops:
**Size**: S
**Reference**: REFERENCE
3. Delete the combination from the B2B shop.
4. Recreate the same combination in the B2B shop.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

Forms in PrestaShop using the POST method are incorrectly submitting data as GET, resulting in form values being appended to the URL. This behavior is unexpected and may cause security issues, as sensitive data may become visible in the URL.

When a merchant has 2 or more currencies, one can set a currency conversion. Lets say NOK and EUR. 
NOK is default price and EUR is set to conversion 0,1, meaning a product priced to 100 NOK, should be converted to 10 EUR. This works fine. 

But when a merchant wants to set the price for EUR specifically, lets say he/she sets it to 8 EUR with a specific price, the automatic currency conversion **should not apply**, however it does. 

In this case the price 8 EUR would be converted to 0,8 EUR.


### Expected behavior

When specific price is set for a currency, automatic currency conversion should not apply.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a product.
2. Activate two or more currencies, set up  currency conversion numbers.
3. Observe in front office that the price change as expected with automatic currency conversion.
4. Now go to the product and set a specific price for a currency.
5. Observe in front office that BOTH your "manual" specific price currency conversion AND the automatic currency conversion is applied.


Now, here is the sollution:
```
classes/Product.php:3896
$id_currency == $specific_price['id_currency'] // instead of strict check $id_currency === $specific_price['id_currency']
```

6. Now observe it works as it should.

The reason is that `$id_currency` is a string and `$specific_price['id_currency']`  is an int (or the other way, I cant remember), so the typesafe condition fails.

The bug should possibly be solved by making sure both those variables are int`s, but a quick fix is to disable the typecheck.

8.1.7

8

title: Add attr_stringify_fetches to PDO init config to avoid BC Break
issue_title: Incompatibility Issue with PDO Returning Integer Values with PHP 8.1
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

 (All PS versions that support PHP 8.1 are affected)

### Describe the bug and add attachments

When using PHP 8.1 with PrestaShop 8.0 (minimal version that support PHP 8.1), the function executeS() from the Db class returns integers for columns that are defined as tinyInt or unsignedInt in the database. In previous PHP versions (before 8.1), the values returned were always strings, regardless of the column type.

This change in behavior is due to PHP 8.1 no longer automatically casting values to strings. Unfortunately, many modules have historically relied on these values being returned as strings, which causes issues when comparing values like '1' === 1.

As a result, module integrations expecting stringified values are disrupted, leading to compatibility issues across PrestaShop versions that support PHP 8.1.

This breaking change is documented here : https://www.php.net/manual/en/migration81.incompatible.php#migration81.incompatible.pdo.sqlite

Exemple with Db->executeS() on ps_product table. 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a232848-bedd-488d-a0a7-f4268b9e220d)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c97d0c1f-286f-40a4-bd96-6d68057fb8b1)


### Expected behavior

The "PDO::ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES" parameter should be set to true on the PDO instance to maintain the historical behavior and avoid breaking changes.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ab8f0b3b-04a1-4532-b58c-efcf70b33296)

### Steps to reproduce

- Run PrestaShop 8.X with PHP 7.4; 
- Dump result of Db-<executeS() query ;
- Run PrestaShop 8.X with PHP 8.1 ;
- Dump result of Db-<executeS() query ;
- Strict compare two result.

### PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened

8.0

8.1

issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

When using product customizations with an additional cost, two issues arise. The additional cost for basic customizations in Prestashop cannot be managed directly, but they can be handled through a custom module by utilizing the id_module and price fields in the customized_data table, which Prestashop automatically uses to calculate the product cost.

# Issue 1: (fixed by https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/36834)
When purchasing a customized item with an extra charge, the "Total products" column on the order confirmation page is incorrect.
Attached are screenshot **01 - Order create.png** and video **01 - Order create.webm**.

# Issue 2: (fixed by https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/36287)
When purchasing the same customized item with two different customizations and two different costs, if I modify the cost of one of the two items in the order, the system updates the cost of both products.
Attached are screenshots **02 - Order edit - 01.png** and **02 - Order edit - 02.png** and video **02 - Order edit.webm**.

Attached is a module that adds 2 customizations to any item added to the cart. Adding the same item twice (with two separate cart additions), the system adds 2 different customizations with 2 different costs.
The module is just an example and with quickly developed code.

### Expected behavior

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce

Issue 1:
1. Access the site and add a product to the cart.

title: Cast OrderProductForViewing - location to string for Memcached
issue_title: Problems OrderProductForViewing "must be of type string (or int), null given" and Memcached
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

I had a problem with retrieving the stock location for products that are no longer available when viewing an old order. Normally, this should return false when the stock location is not found. But when the Memcached cache is active, the null value is returned, causing a fatal error. This must be linked to the fact that Memcached doesn't distinguish between null and false. 

To correct my specific problem, I added the following processing at the end of the setProductCurrentStock() method in /classes/order/Order.php:
```
if ($product['location'] === null) {
    $product['location'] = false;
}
```

This ensures that false is returned and not null. 

The following issues seem to be affected by a similar bug: 
[#22215](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/22215)
[#35753](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/35753)
[#35979](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/35979)

### Expected behavior

_No response_

1. Enable Memcached cache
2. Create an order
3. Delete an ordered product from the catalog

In scenarios where the application is being used in a multilingual context, or when the user's preferred language is different from the default language, this approach leads to incorrect attribute names being fetched and displayed. This can cause confusion for the users and potentially lead to incorrect data handling or display issues in the application. The bug essentially limits the application's flexibility and usability in multilingual environments.

title: PR - Fix order detail price re-calculation
issue_title: Bad price re-calculation on order update from BO
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

When editing an order delivery address in the BO, tthe product prices of that order are recalculated (to adjust the tax for the country). The code is incorrect and DOUBLES the orderDetail->total_price_tax_incl due to a typo.

lease note that this has not been detected earlier because a SECOND update of this order is done later, in the same PHP process, when PrestaShop recalculates all the prices from the products found in the cart, in `OrderAmountUpdater::updateOrderDetails()`

```
ChangeOrderDeliveryAddressHandler::handle()
  `-- OrderDetailUpdater::updateOrderDetailsTaxes()  // first (incorrect) update
  `-- OrderAmountUpdater::update()
        `-- OrderAmountUpdater::updateOrderDetails()  // second update (based on cart product prices)
```


### Expected behavior

Having the good data saved in DB

### Steps to reproduce

0. BEFORE:
have a way to log each SQL request made.
UNRECOMMENDED METHOD: For example, in your ENV environment:
/classes/db/DbPDO.php
```php
   protected function _query($sql)
    {
        try {
            file_put_contents(_PS_ROOT_DIR_.'/pr-fix-order-detail-updater.log', date('[Y-m-d H:i:s] ').print_r($sql, true).PHP_EOL, FILE_APPEND);
            return $this->link->query($sql);
        } catch (PDOException $exception) {
            throw new PrestaShopException($exception->getMessage(), (int) $exception->getCode(), $exception);
        }
    }
```

Steps to reproduce:

1. Have a cart with 2 products, each with an associated VAT tax for your country.
2. Place an order with that cart.
3. in BO, edit the order's delivery address.
4. For example, change the last digit of the phone number.
5. save

You will see in the SQL requests that a first batch of updates is done in `order_detail` with incorrect data, followed by a second batch later on with the correct data

9.0

issue_title: Product Physical quantity in wrongly increased when Order status is changed
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

When an order placed in "Awaiting bank transfer or check payment" status is cancelled (status change) and the order is then set to "Awaiting bank transfer payment" or "Awaiting check payment" status in versions 8... (tested on 8.0.5, 8.1.1, and 8.1.5), the system increases the physical quantity. Here's an example of the incorrect behavior:

Initial stock (physical/reserved/available): 15/0/15.
Order status: Awaiting bank transfer payment -> Physical quantity: 15, Reserved quantity: 1, Available: 14.
The order is cancelled -> Physical quantity: 15, Reserved quantity: 0, Available: 15.
The order is set again to "Awaiting bank transfer payment" or "Awaiting check payment" -> Physical quantity: 16, Reserved quantity: 1, Available: 15.

This incorrect behavior is observed in versions 8... of Prestashop and leads to an incorrect increase in the physical quantity reserved when an order is cancelled and modified again to the "Awaiting bank transfer payment" or "Awaiting check payment" status. It's not acceptable for stock levels to increase in this way; if, for example, an employee mistakenly changes the status to cancelled and then reverts to the initial status, the physical quantity will have increased.

### Expected behavior

I expected that when an order is cancelled and then set back to the "Awaiting bank transfer payment" or "Awaiting check payment" status in Prestashop 8.x, the system should not increase the physical quantity. Instead, the physical quantity should remain the same as before the cancellation.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Place an order in Prestashop 8.x and set the status to "Awaiting bank transfer payment" or "Awaiting check payment".
2. Verify the initial stock levels (physical/reserved/available).
3. Cancel the order.
4. Confirm that the physical quantity remains the same after cancellation.
5. Set the order status back to "Awaiting bank transfer payment" or "Awaiting check payment".
6. Verify the stock levels again and observe that the physical quantity has increased incorrectly.

### PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened

8.0.0 - 8.1.6

title: Removed useless aliases which cause issue with MariaDB
issue_title: MariaDB Incompatibility
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

I am using MariaDB and tried to run the behavioural test suite and get several errors. Around 12 errors are related to a problem with the database and all of the same kind:

````
001 Scenario: one product in cart, quantity 1, can apply only the cart rule which is restricted to selected carrier # Features/Scenario/Cart/CartRule/FrontOffice/carrier.feature:160
      And I save all the restrictions for cart rule cartrule7                                                       # Features/Scenario/Cart/CartRule/FrontOffice/carrier.feature:173
        An exception occurred while executing 'DELETE FROM ps_cart_rule_carrier crc WHERE crc.id_cart_rule = ?' with params [3]:
        
        SQLSTATE[42000]: Syntax error or access violation: 1064 You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that corresponds to your MariaDB server version for the right syntax to use near 'crc WHERE crc.id_cart_rule = '3'' at line 1 (Doctrine\DBAL\Exception\SyntaxErrorException)
````

The cause is, that MariaDB is not supporting an alias for the `DELETE` statement. Minimal test:

````
MariaDB [test_prestashop]> DELETE FROM ps_prodcut xy WHERE id_product=123123;
ERROR 1064 (42000): You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that corresponds to your MariaDB server version for the right syntax to use near 'xy WHERE id_product=123123' at line 1
```` 

I can find a few places where the alias feature is used, but these seem not covered by the automated tests.

When I search MariaDB in the issues, 19 issues are shown. From this, I conclude, that MariaDB is used with PrestaShop and thought to be working. Looking through the issues briefly, I haven't found an indication that MariaDB is not to be used.

The CI tests run only with MySQL.

### Expected behavior

I suggest to do the following, instantly:
- update the documentation stating that: "Only MySQL is fully supported and tested. MariaDB users could run into issues and should report a bug"
- Add a field in the bug report with the database type and version

If MariaDB should be supported, it needs to be added to the CI tests in the long run I think.

Since the problem seems minor and I know what to do now, I will stay with MariaDB in our environment and send some patches.

### Steps to reproduce

Run the behavioural tests with MariaDB

Steps to reproduce : - Go to BO > Attributes page > View `Paper Type` - Click Add new value button - In Attribute group > Change it to `Color` - The inputs for the color attributes are not automatically displayed :x: Same case the other way around. - Go to BO > Attributes page > View `Color` - Click Add new value button - In Attribute group > Change it to `Dimension` - The inputs for the color attributes are not automatically removed :x: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/assets/16019289/e6524081-c975-4c07-bfb8-fd58b6b82b52 - [ ] Fixed ? --- ## Bug 4 The options `Show SQL Query` and `Export to SQL manager` do not work as expected. title: Fix CCC error for path with version
issue_title: 'Version' param from registerJavascript and registerStylesheet break CCC
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

When registering a JavaScript script using `registerJavascript` with a `version` parameter and enabling CCC (Combine, Compress, and Cache) for JavaScript, the generated 'bottom-*.js' file breaks. Instead of including the minified file content, the full path with the version is added to the bottom file. Consequently, this leads to JavaScript errors that disrupt the functionality of all shop JavaScript components.

![image](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/assets/89129201/decf9c32-7c42-4a01-93ba-6da86a316954)

![image](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/assets/89129201/f19349fc-2f91-498a-b12a-f67d609a0c88)



```
$this->context->controller->registerJavascript(
            'module-' . $this->name . '-shop-js',
            'modules/' . $this->name . '/views/js/shop.js',
            [
                'version' => $this->version,
            ]
        );
```

It also does the same with CCC for CSS and registerStylesheet.

While examining the code and the documentation, I also noticed something noteworthy:

- On [this doc page](https://devdocs.prestashop-project.org/8/themes/getting-started/asset-management/), the parameter `attributes` is mentioned.
- However, in [this line of code](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/de990c7031a7833b1d7572f67105b16bae3c6723/classes/assets/CccReducer.php#L108), the parameter is referred to as `attribute`. I realized this because my code previously had `'attribute' => 'async'`, and yet the issue persisted (while the asset should have been ignored if I understood the code correctly). Hence, there may also be a discrepancy regarding this matter.

Many thanks to @NicoVmax who spent some time helping me and who found that the problem was with the 'version' parameter.

@NicoVmax tried this on PS 1.7 and could not reproduce the issue. So maybe it's a regression...

### Expected behavior

The 'bottom-*.js' file should include the minified content of the JavaScript script registered with registerJavascript, regardless of whether a version parameter is provided.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable CCC for JavaScript in the PrestaShop backend.
2. Register a JavaScript script in a module using registerJavascript with a version parameter.
3. Observe the generated 'bottom-*.js' file, noticing the inclusion of the full path with the version instead of the minified file content.
4. Attempt to execute JavaScript functionalities in the shop (product popups, ...), resulting in errors due to the broken script inclusion.

### PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened

8.1.3

### PHP version(s) where the bug happened

PHP 8.1

### If your bug is related to a module, specify its name and its version

Can easily be tested with our module Fintecture on PrestaShop 8.

### Your company or customer's name goes here (if applicable).

Fintecture

title: Fix invoice download for non logged in customer
issue_title: Impossible to download PDF invoice for guest order
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

I'm creating this issue for @Hlavtox.

What's wrong?
- When you want to download an invoice via a standardized link `https://www.domain.com/index.php?controller=pdf-invoice&id_order=XXXX&secure_key=XXXX`, it doesn't work sometimes.
- The condition now says this: `if there is a customer in context and it doesn't match the order customer OR the secure key doesn't match`, die.
- So now if you have a perfectly legit link with secure_key, but you are logged in as different customer or start a guest checkout, the link won't work.
- So the fix is easy, die only if both of these fail:
  - If there is a customer in context and it's not the customer of the order.
  - If there isn't a secure key in the link.

### Expected behavior

I should be able to download the invoice.

### Steps to reproduce

- Make sure that some guest order exists in a shop and invoice is available for it.
- Go to FO, make sure you are logged out. Start a checkout as a guest (without password), no need to fill any addresses.
- Now go to guest tracking and try to track the order and try to download an invoice.
- You will get white screen and `The invoice was not found.`.
- Same situation is when you are logged in in FO as a different customer and you have the link to the invoice in the mail for example.

issue_body:
### Prerequisites

### Describe the bug and add attachments

When you create a product pack and set it's stock type to `Decrement products in pack only.` (`PackStockType::STOCK_TYPE_PRODUCTS_ONLY`) and the quantity of the pack is zero, **it cannot be added to cart**.

### Expected behavior

You MUST be able to add this product to cart even if the quantity is zero.
It worked properly on 1.7.6.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create pack of two standard products, 1 piece of each.
2. Set stock quantity of these two products to 100 each.
3. Go back to the pack, set quantity of the pack to 0, set `Pack quantities` to `Decrement products in pack only`, disable ordering when not in stock.
4. Go to FO and try to add it to cart.
5. Can't be added to cart and no error message is shown. 🔴 
6. Product page shows quantity 0 or nothing, it should show the quantity. 🔴

title: Fix backup tool creating nulls
issue_title: Backup changes data
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

When you make a backup in the Prestashop backoffice it modifies the data that you save by replacing some empty strings with NULL values. Note that this applies to the independent function (advanced settings->database: second tab). The automatic backup during an upgrade uses different code.

In the database the fields isbn, upc and mpn in the ps_product table are declared as default NULL. However, when Prestashop creates products it gives them an empty string value. Yet the backup procedure takes the NULL default as excuse to change empty strings into NULLs.

The problem is that when you do have these values filled with NULL product edit in the backofffice will not work and create a ProductDetails construct crash (see image) with the message: _Argument 2 passed to PrestaShop\PrestaShop\Core\Domain\Product\QueryResult\ProductDetails::__construct() must be of the type string, null given, called in \src\Adapter\Product\QueryHandler\GetProductForEditingHandler.php on line 405_
![nulls](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/assets/13930107/84e9feee-fa4c-42aa-9365-1ba1035d6494)

One situation where this arises is when you make a backup in the backoffice. The backup will look at the field definition and replace empty fields with NULL values.



### Expected behavior

Consist behavior that doesn't cause a crash.

### Steps to reproduce

Make a backup of a PS 8.1 installation. 
Restore the backup and use it as the database.
Edit one of the products

### PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened

8.1

### PHP version(s) where the bug happened

7.4

issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

### Describe the bug and add attachments

When there are no Quick pages created and debug mode is enabled, you get an warning message in almost every page of Backoffice.

This could be easily fixed by modifying these two .tpl files:

- admin-dev/themes/new-theme/template/components/layout/mobile_quickaccess.tpl
- admin-dev/themes/new-theme/template/components/layout/quick_access.tpl

and by wrapping the foreach loops within an if statement, so this:
`{foreach $quick_access as $quick}
......
 {/foreach}`

becomes:

` {if $quick_access}
    {foreach $quick_access as $quick}
....
    {/foreach}
  {/if}`

### Expected behavior

bo pages load correctly

### Steps to reproduce

1. Click on "Manage quick accesses" under the Quick Access menu available on every Backoffice page
![image](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/assets/79152536/6efbdc47-2336-4b39-8a3d-50175ec1c23a)

3. Enable debug mode
4. Go to another Backoffice page, eg. Orders

title: Fix URL with accented chars
issue_title: Persian alphabets changes to English in the URL
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

I upgraded my PrestaShop store, which was in Persian, from 1.7.8.9 to 8.1.1 and found out all the URLs have been changed to English, I have "Accented URL" enabled in the "Traffic & SEO > SEO & URLs menu". We always have to enable this option when we want to have Persian URLs (products, categories, etc.).

I never had this problem in PS 1.6 or 1.7, You would just enable that option and start creating your products with Persian names and friendly URLs, and that's how it should work. Something has changed in PS8 which is absolutely wrong and it's a serious problem for shops that are in Persian.

Here is an example of the changed URL:

Original URL:
`site.com/1-پوشاک-مردانه`

New (**Wrong**) URL:
`site.com/1-pwshak-mrdanh`

It changes every charchter to English, one by one:
پوشاک -> pwshak
پ -> p
و -> w
ش -> sh
ا -> a
ک -> k

The main problem is that URL fields have been changed in the BO. So even if I disable the Accented URL, I can't get my old URLs back, unless there is an option to revert these changes. 

### Expected behavior

It shouldn't convert Persian Charchter to English when "Accented URL" is enabled. I want my URLs to be in Persian.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install PS in Persian (Farsi), or add the Persian language to PS 8.1.1.
2. Enable the Accented URL in the SEO & URLs menu.
3. Create a product combi and write a Persian Name for it. (You can Try "فارسی" which is "Farsi").)

Previous edit: (3. Create a category/product and write a Persian Name for it. (You can Try "فارسی" which is "Farsi").)

(I'm not sure how/when this change applies, I think it takes time to change the URL, or maybe it's related to some sort of cache.)

title: Fix undefined currency if cart is updated before currency is assigned to the context
issue_title: Undefined context currency in actionCartSave
issue_body:
### Describe the bug and add attachments

There is a fatal error if there is a module hooked to `actionCartSave` that is doing something with currency (for example ps_googleanalytics) and the cart needs to be updated on these two places.

https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/5314c7dbc7a745f5d8aed42c681a7b88c6ff1e15/classes/controller/FrontController.php#L361

https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/5314c7dbc7a745f5d8aed42c681a7b88c6ff1e15/classes/controller/FrontController.php#L379


### Stack trace
```
PHP Fatal error: Uncaught PrestaShop\\PrestaShop\\Core\\Localization\\Exception\\LocalizationException: Price specification not found for currency: ""
in /var/www/vhosts/domain.cz/httpdocs/src/Core/Localization/Locale.php:171

Stack trace:
#0 /var/www/vhosts/domain.cz/httpdocs/src/Core/Localization/Locale.php(155): PrestaShop\\PrestaShop\\Core\\Localization\\Locale->getPriceSpecification('')
#1 /var/www/vhosts/domain.cz/httpdocs/classes/Tools.php(776): PrestaShop\\PrestaShop\\Core\\Localization\\Locale->formatPrice(52.231405, NULL)
#2 /var/www/vhosts/domain.cz/httpdocs/classes/Product.php(5567): ToolsCore::displayPrice(52.231405, NULL)
#3 /var/www/vhosts/domain.cz/httpdocs/modules/ps_googleanalytics/classes/Hook/HookActionCartSave.php(96): ProductCore::getProductProperties(1, Array)
#4 /var/www/vhosts/domain.cz/httpdocs/modules/ps_googleanalytics/ps_googleanalytics.php(203): PrestaShop\\Module\\Ps_Googleanalytics\\Hooks\\HookActionCartSave->run()
#5 /var/www/vhosts/kidspara...', referer: https://domain.cz/kosik?action=show
```

### Cause
The issue is caused by currency being initialized at the right place here:

https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/5314c7dbc7a745f5d8aed42c681a7b88c6ff1e15/classes/controller/FrontController.php#L318

But assigned to the context all the way on the bottom:

https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/5314c7dbc7a745f5d8aed42c681a7b88c6ff1e15/classes/controller/FrontController.php#L430

### Solution
Assign currency to the context right away.
PR to fix this: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/33954

### Expected behavior

No error should be thrown

### Steps to reproduce

1. Make sure [tox_carttest.zip](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/files/12718116/tox_carttest.zip) is installed.
2. Go to FO, add two products to cart.
3. Go to cart page.
4. Change language with switcher in header.
5. Error.
6. Apply my PR, it will work fine.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

When setting specific price for a product, if (non default) currency is used in filter, it's not possible to enter new price in "target" currency.

The table shows like it's been set properly, see:

### Expected behavior

Rationale behind this is to allow shop owner set up nicely rounded fixed price for different currencies.

Partial workaround to date is setting up exchange rate to 1:1 with base currency, however that messes up shipping cost.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Import localization pack of another country (e.g. base currency is EUR, import Czech Republic for CZK)

title: Provide rendered category footer
issue_title: Category 'additional description' also shown on paginated pages
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

In PrestaShop 8.1.1
on (product) categories
you can insert a 'description' and an 'additional description'.
Due to SEO-concerns, these descriptions should only be shown on the first page of the product category, not the paginated pages.

However, while the description is in fact only shown on the first page, the 'additional description' is also shown on paginated pages, as shown here:

![chrome_dP5CZcWzmK](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/assets/26773745/c5653913-a59d-472d-a4f5-c384715bbedf)

I checked the templates (in the Classic theme) and found that in fact it should only be listed on the first page:
\themes\classic\templates\catalog\_partials\category-footer.tpl, line 26:
if [...] $listing.pagination.items_shown_from == 1

The same clause is also in the header-template:
\themes\classic\templates\catalog\_partials\category-header.tpl, line 26:
{if $listing.pagination.items_shown_from == 1}
and here its actually working.

So, I guess there must be some bug in the PHP, since the if-clause is not working in category-footer.tpl 

### Expected behavior

The additional description should not be shown on paginated pages.

### Steps to reproduce

In PrestaShop 8.1.1

title: Fix URL sanitization and duplicate language ID
issue_title: URL Alternate with unwanted parameters
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add screenshots

Hello,

I have just discovered an embarrassing SEO bug, which multiplies the number of existing URLs for a page.

This bug concerns the ModuleFrontController (and function hookModuleRoutes) with several languages which are activated on the Prestashop. 

When there is a well-declared rewrite at the module level, such as for the SmartBlog module, the URL generates well with the URL rewrite. However, when Prestashop generates "alternate" URLs, it goes back to the "sanitizeUrl" function, which adds the parameters that are supposed to be hidden.

Here is an example :
```html
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="fr-fr" href="http://www.test.local/fr/blog/category/15_des-conseils.html?slug=des-conseils&module=smartblog">
```




### Expected behavior

We should have :
```html
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="fr-fr" href="http://www.test.local/fr/blog/category/15_des-conseils.html">
```

Checking the code:
https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/531c7407104c4d7cfc72c28808ea9fa80794ff7b/classes/controller/FrontController.php#L2004
We can see that the Sanitize is not useful, because the URL is already generated by Prestashop upstream:
https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/531c7407104c4d7cfc72c28808ea9fa80794ff7b/classes/controller/FrontController.php#L1995

I therefore propose that this sanitize be removed unless there are a few things that escape me.


For my part, I fixed it with an override from a module:
`override/classes/controller/FrontController.php`
```php
<?php

class FrontController extends FrontControllerCore
{
    /**
     * @return array containing the URLs of the same page but for different languages
     */
    protected function getAlternativeLangsUrl()
    {
        $alternativeLangs = [];
        $languages = Language::getLanguages(true, $this->context->shop->id);
        if (count($languages) < 2) {
            return $alternativeLangs;
        }
        foreach ($languages as $lang) {
            $langUrl = $this->context->link->getLanguageLink($lang['id_lang']);
            $alternativeLangs[$lang['language_code']] = $langUrl;
        }
        return $alternativeLangs;
    }
}
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add the SmartBlog module (I think this is a problem with all modules that use ModuleFrontController and the hookModuleRoutes hook)
2. Add at least two languages
3. Create a blog category
4. Check on the category page, Front side, the "alternate" tag

1.7.8.5

### PHP version(s) where the bug happened

7.4

issue_title: Prevent directory listings in the htaccess for Apache
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

### Describe the bug and add attachments

Some hosting providers, by default, do not prevent directory listings. We frequently encounter merchants whose directories can be viewed because of the absence of an `index.php` file, particularly when their hosting hasn't been configured correctly to restrict directory listings. Consequently, when these directories are accessed online, a list of files becomes visible. This poses a security risk, especially in cases where custom directories contain configuration files or other resources that shouldn't be publicly accessible.

### Expected behavior

The directly listing should be prevented in the htaccess.

### Steps to reproduce

To reproduce the issue, the Apache server should not enforce the Indexes.

title: Prevent removing non restricted cart rules
issue_title: Deleting !LoadedObject Customer deletes all CartRules that don't have customer restrictions
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

This does not happen in regular use but happens when someone (me) does integration without checking everything all the time (which is way too easy)

Take this code:

```php
$Customer = new Customer(-1);
$Customer->delete();
```

delete does not complain anything BUT there is a side effect!

Customer::delete https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/65e20f37cfe40d4ad47480ada09c4fc45a4fa0f0/classes/Customer.php#L416

Does `CartRule::deleteByIdCustomer((int) $this->id);` but because the Customer was not really loaded (id -1 does not exists) the Customer object id is `null` but casting null to int makes it zero...

https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/65e20f37cfe40d4ad47480ada09c4fc45a4fa0f0/classes/CartRule.php#L614

`deleteByIdCustomer` does not check for 0 being a case and selects all CartRules where id_customer==0 and happily deletes them.

### Expected behavior

* Calling $Object->delete() when object is not valid loaded object should fail.
* `deleteByIdCustomer` should never be able to delete CartRules that do not have Customer condition set (e.g id_customer is 0)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create CartRules with and withourt customer conditions
2. run the code above

=> all CartRules that didn't have customer conditions set are deleted

### PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened

1.7.8.0

title: Refacto getShopLogo remove hasKey usage
issue_title: Configuration::haskey is ignorant of multishop configuration
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

The call of `Configuration::haskey` without the optional `$id_shop` returns false if the key exists in the current shop context, but does not exist as default configuration (`select * from ps_configuration where id_shop is null and id_shop_group is null and name ='[configuration name]'`).

### Expected behavior

I expect for `Configuration::haskey('[configuration name]')` to return true, if we are in a specific shop context and that configuration exists in that shop.

I already found twice code in PrestaShop, that expects this function to return true in the case that a configuration exists in the current shop context.

The code in `FrontController::getShopLogo()` is an example:
```
    public function getShopLogo(): array
    {
        if (!Configuration::hasKey('PS_LOGO')) {
            return [];
        }

        $logoFileName = Configuration::get('PS_LOGO');
```
Here `Configuration::get('PS_LOGO')` looks up the configuration in the current shop context, but `Configuration::hasKey('PS_LOGO')` does not take in account the current shop context.

Another example where `Configuration::haskey` is wrongly used is https://github.com/202-ecommerce/paypal/issues/121.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install a Prestashop multi-shop environment as described in https://gist.github.com/lmeyer1/c40a19d880758bee11a1e8a2c5e819c3
2. In __Design - Theme & Logo__ set a logo file for each shop.
3. Connect to phpmyadmin (localhost:8018 is installed following 1.)
4. Run the query `select * from ps_configuration where name = 'PS_LOGO';`, and notice that there are now 4 keys: one for each of the three shops and a default for `id_shop is null and id_shop_group is null`
5. Delete the row with the (now unused) default value (query `delete from ps_configuration where id_shop is null and id_shop_group is null and name ='PS_LOGO'`)
6. Navigate to any page in the FO. You notice either:
   - a missing logo
   - an error 500 related to the missing logo (I noticed it with classic theme in the checkout)

1.7.8.7

7.3

title: Profiler: measure execution time from the beginning.
issue_title: Profiler shows incorrect execution time
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

When using the Profiler, I notice that the execution time is wrong.
In fact the start_time is when `Profiler::__construct` is called https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/ff3780e47ad5ff031440c6856f6ec031801de0d3/tools/profiling/Profiler.php#L76,
but it should be the start of the request, when `index.php` is starting to execute.

![Immagine 2023-05-30 153824](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/assets/7520695/82cb86cf-c377-4b68-b386-7ece557efb30)

In this image, the three numbers displayed at the top are `{$smarty.server.REQUEST_TIME_FLOAT} {$run.startTime}
  {load_time data=($run.startTime - $smarty.server.REQUEST_TIME_FLOAT)}` added in https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/tools/profiling/templates/run.tpl

This proves that there are 91ms that are used by the initialisation of Prestashop before `Profiler::__construct()`

### Expected behavior

In the profiler, the time should start to run when the script starts executing.
This would be the good starting time on which the calculations for the profiler should be base on: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/ff3780e47ad5ff031440c6856f6ec031801de0d3/config/config.inc.php#L38
If the server exposes the variable `$_SERVER['REQUEST_TIME_FLOAT']`, then this would also be a good candidate as start time.


The correct value for `config` Time in the image above should be 5.611ms + 91.627ms = 97.238ms

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable profiling in `defines_custom.inc.php` by adding `define('_PS_DEBUG_PROFILING_', true);`
2. In https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/ff3780e47ad5ff031440c6856f6ec031801de0d3/tools/profiling/templates/run.tpl#L26, before the `<table>` add `{$smarty.server.REQUEST_TIME_FLOAT} {$run.startTime}
  {load_time data=($run.startTime - $smarty.server.REQUEST_TIME_FLOAT)}`
3. Load a page in the front end and look at the output of the Profiler

8.0.4 and devel

title: Fix error when change product qty in cart

issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

In the cart page, if you have a product with quantity greater than the established in stock available a error shows up stating:
'product x' is no longer available in this quantity. You cannot proceed with your order until the quantity is adjusted.

If you proceed to reduce the quantity in the quantity input, the cart will not allow it showing :
The available purchase order quantity for this product is 'x'.
And reverts back the previous quantity value

This always happens with products without attribute, if the product is with attribute, it will allow the reduction of quantity only if the change is less or equal than the stock available.


### Expected behavior

When the quantity of a product in the cart is less than the available quantity and the user presses the "Order" button in the cart, a message is displayed: "The available quantity for the order of this product is X" and the product quantity is set to the quantity available X.

If the user presses the up key or types a quantity greater than the available quantity, the quantity is reset to the available quantity.
if the user presses the down key or types a quantity equal to or less than the available quantity, the quantity value is not updated.

### Steps to reproduce

With the demo store:

1. Go to the product 7 page ('Mug The adventure begins') and add 5 items to your cart
2. In the admin modify the stock of this product in such a way that only 3 are left available
3. Back in the front go to the cart page and you will see the error message, and the product with the quantity of 5 that you requested
4. Try to reduce the quantity, is not possible

8.1.0

Within early PrestaShop 1.7
```none

```none
PHP Warning:  Trying to access array offset on value of type int
```

The fallback value after the warnings is always `NULL` and it is used to construct the default `new Category` object in the Dashboardproducts module.


### Expected behavior

`Product->getDefaultCategory` may return either a string, an int or an array with an `id_category_default` key, when SQL value is found \(due to another bug in `ProductCore->getDefaultCategory` which uses `Db::getInstance()->getValue` and proceeds like it would return a result array from PDO or MySQLI.

Due to the upstream core bug in the `Product->getDefaultCategory`, the returned value has to be checked for type and handled accordingly. \(_to maintain backward compatibility with the Core bug and plan forward compatibility for when the Core bug patch PrestaShop/PrestaShop#31752 can be merged_).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open backoffice Dashboard
2. Open server logs and see the PHP Warning

title: Use index for connections.date_add
issue_title: Incorrect condition disallows use of index `date_add` on table `ps_connections`
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

The display of the Carts page in the BO takes a lot of time (often it delays after the timeout of 300 s). The query used is 

```
SELECT a.`id_cart`, a.`date_add` AS `date_add` , CONCAT(LEFT(c.`firstname`, 1), '. ', c.`lastname`) `customer`, a.id_cart total, ca.name carrier, o.id_order, IF ( IFNULL(o.id_order, 'Non commandé') = 'Non commandé', IF(TIME_TO_SEC(TIMEDIFF('2023-03-03 09:08:00', a.`date_add`)) > 86400, 'Panier abandonné', 'Non commandé'), o.id_order ) AS status, IF(o.id_order, 1, 0) badge_success, IF(o.id_order, 0, 1) badge_danger, IF(co.id_guest, 1, 0) id_guest, shop.name as shop_name 
FROM `ps_cart` a 
LEFT JOIN ps_customer c ON (c.id_customer = a.id_customer) 
LEFT JOIN ps_currency cu ON (cu.id_currency = a.id_currency) 
LEFT JOIN ps_carrier ca ON (ca.id_carrier = a.id_carrier) 
LEFT JOIN ps_orders o ON (o.id_cart = a.id_cart) 
LEFT JOIN ( SELECT DISTINCT `id_guest` FROM `ps_connections` 
WHERE TIME_TO_SEC(TIMEDIFF('2023-03-03 09:08:00', `date_add`)) < 1800 ) AS co ON co.`id_guest` = a.`id_guest` 
LEFT JOIN `ps_shop` shop ON a.`id_shop` = shop.`id_shop` 
WHERE 1 AND a.id_shop IN (20) ORDER BY a.id_cart DESC LIMIT 0, 50;
```
Notice the inner select `SELECT DISTINCT id_guest FROM ps_connections WHERE TIME_TO_SEC(TIMEDIFF('2023-03-03 09:08:00', date_add)) < 1800`. The table ps_connections does have an index on the field `date_add`, but with this condition it cannot be used. In fact the calculation must be executed for each of the lines in ps_connections (these can be tens or hundreds of thousnad).

### Expected behavior

The condition in the query should be turned around in a way that the calculation is only done once. For instance: 
```
`date_add` > date_add(now(), interval -30 minute))
```
That way the index `date_add` on the table `ps_connections` can be used and the query time drops into fractions of a second.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In the BO, navigate to `Orders - Carts`
2. Notice that the page takes a long time to load.

Note: my `ps_connections` table has 2M+ rows

### PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened

8.0.1 and develop

### PHP version(s) where the bug happened

any

title: Take locale into account when deciding whether module translation should fall back to the legacy system
issue_title: Translation locale override doesn't work if translation is missing for default language
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add attachments

If you pass the optional `$locale` parameter to `trans()`, the function still returns the translation in the default language unless a translation also exists in the default language in the database. So if your default locale is English but you want your translation to always show up in Finnish, the translation needs to exist in both languages in the database for it to show up in Finnish.

### Expected behavior

The translation should be returned in the desired language regardless of whether a translation exists in the default one.

This used to work in PrestaShop versions <8.0.1.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Download and install [this test module](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/files/10901709/localetest.zip)
2. Set your back office language to English
3. Download and install the Finnish language pack OR modify the trans() function call in the test module to use another language that you already have installed
4. Translate the test string (in domain "Modules.Localetest.Test") to Finnish or the language you used for the override (you can translate it to whatever, the string just needs to be different)
5. DO NOT translate the test string in English
6. Go to the test module configuration page and see that the test string is still in English

### PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened

8.0.1

7.2.34
